忠義五
Loyalty and Righteousness, Part 5

王淑元高延祉黃為錦瑞麟曹燮培楊映河等
Wang Shuyuan, Gao Yanzhi, Huang Wei, Jin Ruilin, Cao Xiepei, Yang Yinghe, and others

劉繼祖翟登峨等劉作肅沈衍慶李仁元李福培王恩綬
Liu Jizu, Zhai Deng'e, and others; Liu Zuosu, Shen Yanqing, Li Renyuan, Li Fupei, and Wang Enshou

李右文從弟載文李榞陳肖儀萬成袁祖德李大均
Li Youwen; his younger cousin Zaiwen; Li Yuan; Chen Xiaoyi; Wan Cheng; Yuan Zude; and Li Dajun
6
於松尚那布李淮唐治鍾普塘等林源恩唐德昇
Yu Song, Shangnabu, Li Huai, Tang Zhi, Zhong Putang, and others; Lin Yuan'en and Tang Desheng
7
畢大鈺湯世銓劉福林謝子澄周憲曾等文穎徐鳳喈等
Bi Dayu, Tang Shiquan, Liu Fulin, Xie Zicheng, Zhou Xianzeng, and others; Wen Ying, Xu Fengjie, and others

張積功傅士珍瞿濬冒芬施作霖韓體震德克登額
Zhang Jigong, Fu Shizhen, Qu Jun, Mao Fen, Shi Zuolin, Han Tizhen, and Deke Deng'e

蔣嘉穀鄧玲筠承順托克清阿馮元吉
Jiang Jiagu, Deng Lingyun, Chengshun Tuokeqing'a, and Feng Yuanji
10
平源張寶華王泗週來豫餘寶錕王汝揆
Pingyuan, Zhang Baohua, Wang Si, Zhou Laiyu, Yu Baokun, and Wang Ruokui
11
王淑元，字秋查，浙江鄞縣人。 以舉人知縣，分發廣西。 歷權柳城、雒容、平南、馬平等縣事，授博平，調天保。 會臨桂縣民以糧價重不輸稅，大吏欲懾以兵，淑元在省，進議曰：「民固有所苦，得平自服。 」遂調臨桂。 既蒞任，為汰浮收，民便之，無逋賦者。
Wang Shuyuan, styled Qiucha, came from Yin County in Zhejiang. Having passed the provincial examinations, he received a county magistracy and was posted to Guangxi. He served in turn as acting magistrate of Liucheng, Luorong, Pingnan, and Maping, was appointed to Boping, and was then transferred to Tianbao. When the people of Lingui County stopped paying taxes because grain prices were too high, senior officials wanted to intimidate them with troops. Shuyuan was at the provincial seat and advised: "The people must have real hardships; treat them fairly and they will comply on their own." He was accordingly transferred to Lingui. After he assumed office, he cut out padded collections, which eased the burden on the people, and tax arrears disappeared.
12
道光季年，粵匪洪秀全始謀逆，其黨李嘉耀潛入省垣煽土匪內應，發覺，淑元鞫得餘匪匿所，悉數掩擒，敘功昇龍州同知，以肅清會匪獎知府銜。 二十九年，擢太平府知府，旋任龍州。 時廣西巡撫鄭祖琛懦而黯，群盜蜂起，輒務諱匿。 三十年，賊潘寶源等來犯，淑元率練丁禦諸距州十里之灣道，以次子光頡自隨。 戰不利，雨甚，藥濕砲不及發，因退回城。 及門，賊已由間道入，擁眾逼官廨。 淑元立堂上，罵不絕口，呼家眾殺賊。 賊斫淑元僕地，擄之去，光頡奔奪，賊殺光頡，而投淑元於勤村河。 盜去三日，始出之，身首皆裂，獨面色如生。
In the last years of Daoguang, Hong Xiuquan of Guangdong first began plotting rebellion. His associate Li Jiayao slipped into the provincial capital to stir up local bandits for an internal rising, but the plot was uncovered. Shuyuan examined the prisoners, learned where the remaining rebels were hidden, and seized them all. He was promoted to subprefect of Longzhou and given the nominal rank of prefect for clearing out secret-society bandits. In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to prefect of Taiping and shortly afterward assumed duties at Longzhou. The Guangxi governor at the time, Zheng Zuchen, was timid and evasive; as bandits rose on every side, he habitually tried to cover it up. In the thirtieth year Pan Baoyuan and other rebels attacked. Shuyuan led local militia to meet them at Wandao, ten li from the city, with his second son Guangjie at his side. The fight went against them. Heavy rain had soaked the gunpowder, so the guns could not be fired, and they fell back to the city. By the time they reached the gate, the rebels had already come in by a side route and were crowding the government compound. Shuyuan stood in the main hall, hurling unending abuse, and ordered his household to kill the rebels. The rebels cut Shuyuan down and dragged him away. Guangjie rushed to save him; the rebels killed Guangjie and threw Shuyuan into the Qincun River. Only three days after the rebels departed was his body recovered. Head and trunk were mangled, but his face looked as though he were still alive.
13
高延祉，字筠坡，浙江蕭山人。 由舉人充官學教習，期滿，用知縣。 道光二十一年，英夷犯浙江沿海，舉行團練，延祉率義勇為前驅，擊毀夷船。 咸豐元年，揀發廣西，與都下親友別，即以致身奉國自誓。 尋署隆安縣事，土賊陸鵬理與其黨乃利中、凌阿東等，屢為邑害。 延祉集團練，遣間諜，以計誘殺鵬理，捕獲其家屬黨與二十餘人，並毀利中巢窟及塚。 阿東亡命，謀復仇，糾眾千餘，據白山之感墟，與歸德接壤。 延祉偕歸德土知州黃為錦率練勇四百進攻，沿途搜戮賊探多名，行抵袍墟，距感墟十餘裡，遇伏，軍潰。 复激勵練勇奮擊，殪匪二百餘。 賊眾蜂至，延祉挺刃督戰，被賊矛中腹遇害，為錦亦戰死，僕隸多殉之者。
Gao Yanzhi, styled Yunpo, came from Xiaoshan in Zhejiang. A provincial graduate, he served as an instructor in the Imperial Academy, and when his term expired he was appointed a county magistrate. In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, when the British attacked the Zhejiang coast, Yanzhi led local volunteers in the vanguard and destroyed enemy vessels. In the first year of Xianfeng he was posted to Guangxi. As he left friends and family in the capital, he swore to give his life for the country. He soon took charge of Long'an County, where local bandits led by Lu Pengli, along with Nai Lizhong, Ling Adong, and others, had long plagued the area. Yanzhi raised militia, sent spies, and by a ruse lured Lu Pengli to his death. He captured more than twenty of Pengli's family and followers and destroyed Lizhong's stronghold and tomb. Adong went into hiding and plotted revenge, mustering more than a thousand men at Ganxu on White Mountain, on the border with Guide. Yanzhi joined Huang Wei, the native magistrate of Guide, in leading four hundred militiamen in an assault. Along the march they hunted down many rebel scouts. At Paoxu, a little over ten li from Ganxu, they walked into an ambush and the column broke. He rallied the militia again for a fierce counterattack and killed more than two hundred rebels. Rebels poured in from every side. Yanzhi drew his sword and led the fight, but a rebel spear pierced his belly and killed him. Wei also fell in battle, and many of their servants died with them.
14
延祉任隆安七十餘日，無日不在外治戰事，居縣廨僅數日耳。 民感其保衛之恩，爭賻其孤，孤； 乃以其貲建祠祀之，以從死之僕隸、壯勇附。 同治十一年，追諡壯節。
In his seventy-odd days at Long'an, Yanzhi was in the field every day and spent only a few days in the county yamen. Grateful for his defense of them, the people competed to give to his orphaned children. From those gifts they built a shrine in his honor, with the servants and militiamen who died with him enshrined beside him. In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he was posthumously honored as Zhuangjie.
15
為錦，山東人。
Huang Wei was from Shandong.
16
瑞麟，白氏，漢軍鑲白旗人。 由謄錄議敘巡檢，道光五年，選廣西鎮峽寨巡檢。 調主簿，擢州判、知州。 咸豐元年，授西隆州知州。 咸豐二年二月，洪秀全自永安犯桂林，敗竄全州，瑞麟已卸州事，繼任知州曹燮培知瑞麟才，深相結納，約共守禦。 時都司武昌顯以楚兵四百援桂林，道經全州，燮培留助守。 四月，賊薄城下，發砲轟擊，斃賊甚夥。 越日攻益急，歷十一晝夜，提督餘萬清、劉長清來援，分駐城北太平堡，城西魯班橋，距十五里外，牽制弗能進，守者憊甚，子藥不繼。 賊穴城，地雷發，城崩，賊乘入，千總葉永林、把總張元福死之。 瑞麟素驍勇，遇賊中衢，手刃數人，力竭身死。 燮培亦巷戰死。
Ruilin, of the Bai clan, was a Hanjun bondservant of the Bordered White Banner. He rose through transcription service to an assistant magistracy, and in the fifth year of Daoguang was appointed to Zhenxia Stockade in Guangxi. He was moved to registrar, then promoted through subprefect to prefect. In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Xilong. In the second month of the second year of Xianfeng, Hong Xiuquan advanced from Yong'an on Guilin, was beaten, and fled toward Quanzhou. Ruilin had already left office, but his successor Cao Xiepei, recognizing his talent, drew close to him and pledged to defend the city together. The commandant Wu Changxian was then marching four hundred Chu troops to relieve Guilin. Xiepei kept him at Quanzhou to help hold the city. In the fourth month the rebels closed on the walls. Cannon fire killed great numbers of them. The attack intensified the next day. For eleven days and nights Generals Yu Wanqing and Liu Changqing tried to relieve the city from Taiping Fort to the north and Luban Bridge to the west, fifteen li away, but could not break through. The defenders were exhausted and ran out of ammunition. The rebels tunneled under the wall; a mine brought it down, and they poured in. Battalion officer Ye Yonglin and platoon officer Zhang Yuanfu were killed. Ruilin had always been a fierce fighter. He met the rebels in the main street, cut down several with his own blade, and fell when his strength failed. Xiepei too died fighting in the alleys.
17
賊攻城時，多死傷，恨甚，城陷，屠之，焚屋舍幾盡。 文武官紳同時死者：署全州營參將楊映河，把總卜有祥，解餉官四川知縣盧金第，安徽府經歷陳堯，湖南游擊餘遇升，都司武昌顯，千總田慶華、馬瑞龍，把總盧先振、黃志林、韓大興，外委孫紹全、楊清麒、田宏義、楊大賓、龔心仁、田宗南，武舉唐殿試，生員蔣成龍、金建勳，武生張以敬，幕友黃柏彬、祝永文、硃福坪、周希齡、孫培駒、楊菱舟、金家駒、硃澤，凡三十餘人。 學正農賢託，年七十，甫歿，棺毀，妻殉之。 瑞麟諡壯節，與燮培並贈道銜，詔祀京師昭忠祠。 建專祠全州，曰愍忠，祀燮培及諸死事者。
The rebels had taken heavy losses in the siege and hated the city fiercely. When it fell they slaughtered the people and burned almost every building. Among the more than thirty civil and military officials and local notables who died at the same time were acting brigade commander Yang Yinghe of the Quanzhou garrison; platoon officer Bu Youxiang; pay convoy official and Sichuan magistrate Lu Jindi; Anhui prefectural registrar Chen Yao; Hunan brigade commander Yu Yusheng; commandant Wu Changxian; battalion officers Tian Qinghua and Ma Ruilong; platoon officers Lu Xianzhen, Huang Zhilin, and Han Daxing; junior officers Sun Shaoquan, Yang Qingqi, Tian Hongyi, Yang Dabin, Gong Xinren, and Tian Zongnan; military licentiate Tang Dianshi; students Jiang Chenglong and Jin Jianxun; military student Zhang Yijing; and secretaries Huang Baobin, Zhu Yongwen, Zhu Fuping, Zhou Xiling, Sun Peiju, Yang Lingzhou, Jin Jiaju, and Zhu Ze. The director of studies Nong Xiantuo, seventy years old, had only just died; his coffin was smashed, and his wife died with him. Ruilin was posthumously titled Zhuangjie. He and Xiepei were both granted the nominal rank of circuit intendant and ordered enshrined in the Capital Shrine of Manifest Loyalty. A dedicated shrine called Minzhong was built at Quanzhou to honor Xiepei and all who died in the defense.
18
燮培，字理村，浙江仁和人。 選柳州通判，攝西隆州、賓州事，除東蘭州知州，權全州。 性倜儻，有吏才，不拘節目，聲伎滿前，然無廢事。 或規之，引文信國公少年時事自解，曰：「他日能學文山足矣！ 」人謂燮培無負素志雲。
Cao Xiepei, styled Licun, came from Renhe in Zhejiang. He was appointed subprefect of Liuzhou, served in turn as acting prefect of Xilong and Bin, was appointed prefect of Donglan, and finally acted as prefect of Quanzhou. He was unconventional and capable in office. He cared little for formal routine; musicians and performers filled his hall, yet he never let official business slide. When others reproved him, he pointed to the Duke of Xin's youthful excesses and said: "If I can one day live up to Wenshan, that will be enough!" People said Xiepei had not betrayed that early vow.
19
時死廣西者，又有署永安州吳江龍門司巡檢馮元等。
Others who died in Guangxi at this time included Feng Yuan, acting assistant magistrate of Longmen in Wujiang under Yong'an, and others.
20
劉繼祖，江西玉山人。 增貢生。 道光十一年，以同知分福建。 十九年，除淡水同知，以憂去。 服闋，借揀知州，發廣西。 二十七年，授永康，尋署藤縣。 時灌陽、平樂、陽朔等處匪徒肆擾，偕知府張熙宇督剿，殲擒殆盡，進知府。 咸豐元年，金田賊敗竄大黃江，繼祖率水陸壯勇乘夜攻擊，焚其巢。 以所部練勇失鈐束，奪職。 四年，巡撫勞崇光奏請留藤協辦團練，尋艇賊梁培友糾眾攻藤，繼祖偕知縣翟登峨等嬰城固守，設間出奇擊卻之。 旋以土賊馮六、戴九等接踵至，據河干，盡焚沿岸舟，鄉團來援者不得渡。 賊眾兵單，城陷，繼祖受重創，與登峨子襄採、團長梁文軾等巷戰，力竭，死之。 登峨被擄，罵賊不屈，被害，棄屍於河。 典史冉正棠鬥死獄門。 詔复繼祖原官，賞世職，登峨以次死者卹有差。
Liu Jizu came from Yushan in Jiangxi. He held senior tribute-student status. In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was posted to Fujian as a subprefect. In the nineteenth year he was appointed subprefect of Tamsui, then left office to observe mourning. After mourning he was provisionally appointed prefect and sent to Guangxi. In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed to Yongkang and soon took charge of Teng County. Bandits were then ravaging Guanyang, Pingle, Yangshuo, and neighboring districts. With Prefect Zhang Xiyu he led the suppression, killing or capturing nearly all of them, and was promoted to prefect. In the first year of Xianfeng the defeated Jintian rebels fled to the Dahuang River. Jizu led land and river forces in a night assault and burned their camp. His militia had gotten out of hand, and he was dismissed from office. In the fourth year Governor Lao Chongguang asked that he stay at Teng to help organize militia. Soon the river pirate Liang Peiyou gathered men to attack the county. Jizu joined Magistrate Zhai Deng'e in a desperate defense and used a ruse to launch a surprise attack that beat the enemy back. Then local bandits Feng Liu, Dai Jiu, and others arrived in turn, seized the riverbank, burned every boat along the shore, and cut off the village militia trying to cross to help. The rebels outnumbered the defenders, and the city fell. Jizu was badly wounded and, with Deng'e's son Xiangcai and militia leader Liang Wenqian, fought street by street until he was spent and died. Deng'e was taken captive. He cursed the rebels and refused to submit; they killed him and threw his body into the river. Clerk Ran Zhengtang died fighting at the prison gate. An edict restored Jizu to his former rank and granted a hereditary office. Deng'e and the others who died received posthumous honors according to their stations.
21
登峨，字眉峰，山東章丘人。 進士，截取選藤縣。
Zhai Deng'e, styled Meifeng, came from Zhangqiu in Shandong. A jinshi, he was specially appointed magistrate of Teng County.
22
劉作肅，字敬亭，奉天承德縣人。 道光元年舉人，選知縣，授天河縣。 歷寧明知州，兼明江同知。 咸豐三年，賊眾萬餘攻城，相持五月餘，解圍去。 以城守功加知府，賞花翎。 六年，署太平知府，賊屢來犯，禦卻之。 十年，復來。 城中無儲粟，賊圍亟，守陴者皆走。 城陷，作肅投池，水淺，不能死，為賊擁去。 以其居官清廉，不忍害之。 作肅乃吟絕命辭，絕粒死。 其弟與僕姚云、吳貴同殉。 妻趙及子家祥、女等皆先自盡。 以子家鳳被執不屈死，卹如製。 賞世職，建祠府城，二僕並賜卹。
Liu Zuosu, styled Jingting, came from Chengde County in Fengtian. A provincial graduate of the first year of Daoguang, he was appointed magistrate of Tianhe County. He served as prefect of Ningming and concurrently as subprefect of Mingjiang. In the third year of Xianfeng more than ten thousand rebels besieged the city for over five months before breaking off and leaving. For defending the city he was promoted to prefect and awarded a peacock feather. In the sixth year he served as acting prefect of Taiping and repeatedly beat back rebel attacks. In the tenth year they returned. The city had no grain in store. The siege tightened, and the defenders on the walls fled. When the city fell, Zuosu threw himself into a pond, but the water was too shallow to drown him, and the rebels dragged him away. Knowing how honest he had been in office, they could not bring themselves to kill him. Zuosu then composed a final poem and starved himself to death. His younger brother and his servants Yao Yun and Wu Gui died with him. His wife Zhao, his son Jiaxiang, his daughters, and others had already taken their own lives. Because his son Jiafeng had been captured, refused to submit, and was killed, the family received the full statutory honors. A hereditary office was granted, a shrine was built in the prefectural seat, and the two servants received posthumous honors as well.
23
沈衍慶，字槐卿，安徽石埭人。 道光十五年進士，以知縣發江西，署興國，補泰和。 二十五年，調鄱陽，縣濱湖，盜賊所出沒。 衍慶編漁戶，仿保甲法行之，屢獲劇盜。 俗悍好鬥，輒輕騎馳往，竭誠開導，事浸息。 兩遇水災，盡力賑撫，存活無算。 舉卓異。 咸豐二年，粵匪陷湖北武昌，衍慶請兵守康山，控鄱陽門戶。 三年，九江陷，譌言四起，居民逃亡，不可禁止。 衍慶率練勇巡東門，見糧船中數百人譟而前，衍慶手刃二人，餘黨慴服，人心始定。 賊圍南昌，巡撫張芾檄衍慶赴援，會合省防諸軍與賊戰，大破之。 賊將東竄，衍慶慮賊犯鄱陽，請於巡撫，馳歸。 時樂平令李仁元攝鄱陽事，同商守禦。 賊至，與仁元同力戰，城陷，死之。 贈道銜，立祠鄱陽。
Shen Yanqing, styled Huaiqing, came from Shidi in Anhui. A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Daoguang, he was posted to Jiangxi as a county magistrate, served at Xingguo, and was appointed to Taihe. In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Poyang, a lakefront county where bandits came and went. Yanqing organized the fishing households on the baojia model and repeatedly captured major bandits. The people were fierce and quick to fight. He would ride out with only a light escort, counsel them earnestly, and gradually the violence died down. Twice floods struck the county, and he threw himself into relief work, saving countless lives. He was cited for outstanding service. In the second year of Xianfeng, when Guangdong rebels seized Wuchang in Hubei, Yanqing asked for troops to hold Kangshan and guard the approach to Poyang. In the third year Jiujiang fell. Rumors spread everywhere, and the people fled in panic that could not be checked. Yanqing led militia on patrol at the east gate and saw several hundred men in grain boats rushing forward in uproar. He cut down two with his own blade; the rest submitted, and the town settled down. When rebels besieged Nanchang, Governor Zhang Fu summoned Yanqing to help. He joined the provincial forces, fought the enemy, and won a major victory. As the rebels prepared to flee east, Yanqing feared they would strike Poyang, obtained leave from the governor, and rode home at once. The magistrate of Leping, Li Renyuan, was then acting for Poyang, and the two planned the defense together. When the rebels arrived, he fought beside Renyuan with all his might. The city fell, and he was killed. He was granted the nominal rank of circuit intendant, and a shrine was erected at Poyang.
24
仁元，字資齋，河南濟源人。 道光二十七年進士，內閣中書，改知縣。 咸豐元年，授樂平。 民俗剽悍，以禮讓教之，多感悟。 有素習械鬥者，仁元曰：「民不畏死，然後可以致死。 今天下多事，正此輩效順之時也。 」簡驍健得六百人，日加訓練，土匪畏之，斂跡。 樂平與鄱陽為鄰境，仁元政聲亦與衍慶相埒，至是南昌戒嚴，衍慶助剿，仁元移攝鄱陽以代之。 未幾，衍慶以防賊擾，馳歸縣。 因仁元父母妻子在樂平，亟趣仁元去。 仁元曰：「賊旦夕且至，臨敵易令，是謂我不丈夫也。 」遂議並力戰守。 值久雨湖漲，城圮，無險可攖。 於是審度地勢，衍慶軍南門，仁元軍北門，為犄角。 部署甫定，賊揚帆大至。 麾軍燃砲，碎賊艦，賊繞東門登岸，入城，衍慶迎擊，賊稍卻。 又繞而北，仁元率樂平勇巷戰，矛刺仁元，踣，臠割之。 所部猶力戰，死者過半，卒得仁元屍以出。
Li Renyuan, styled Zizhai, came from Jiyuan in Henan. A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, he served in the Grand Secretariat and then became a county magistrate. In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed magistrate of Leping. The people were fierce and quarrelsome. He taught them courtesy and restraint, and many were moved to change. Some were habitual fighters. Renyuan said: "Only those who do not fear death can be asked to risk their lives." "The empire is in turmoil; this is the moment for such men to serve loyally." He picked six hundred strong men and drilled them daily. Local bandits feared them and kept quiet. Leping bordered Poyang, and Renyuan's reputation matched Yanqing's. When Nanchang went on alert, Yanqing went to help fight the rebels, and Renyuan took charge at Poyang in his stead. Soon Yanqing, fearing an attack on Poyang, rode back in haste. Since Renyuan's parents, wife, and children were still at Leping, he urged him to go at once. Renyuan said: "The enemy may come at any moment. To change command on the eve of battle would be unworthy of a man." They agreed to defend the city together. Long rains had swollen the lake, the walls had crumbled, and there was no defensible ground left. They surveyed the ground and posted Yanqing at the south gate and Renyuan at the north, supporting each other like pincers. They had barely finished deploying when a great rebel fleet bore down under sail. He ordered the guns fired and smashed rebel ships. The enemy landed at the east gate and entered the city. Yanqing counterattacked and drove them back briefly. They swung north again. Renyuan led the Leping militia in street fighting until a spear brought him down; the rebels hacked his body apart. His men kept fighting; more than half were killed, but they finally recovered Renyuan's body and carried it out.
25
初，樂平土匪度仁元去必復來，伏不敢動。 及聞殉難，乃倡議迎賊。 仁元母顧其婦及女曰：「禍將及矣，曷早計！ 」皆死之。 城陷，仁元父及弟並不屈死。 事聞，詔贈知府銜。 與衍慶合祠於鄱陽，別於樂平建仁元專祠，父予墀、母陳氏、妻金氏、弟誠元、妹三人、妾楊氏及僕、婦等均附祀。
At first the Leping bandits assumed Renyuan would return once he left, so they lay low. When they heard he had been killed, they proposed welcoming the rebels. Renyuan's mother turned to his wife and daughters and said: "Disaster is coming—act now!" They all took their own lives. When the city fell, Renyuan's father and younger brother also refused to yield and were killed. When word reached the court, he was granted the nominal rank of prefect. He was enshrined with Yanqing at Poyang. A separate shrine to Renyuan was built at Leping, where his father Yu Chi, mother Lady Chen, wife Lady Jin, brother Chengyuan, three sisters, concubine Lady Yang, and servants and attendants were honored as well.
26
李福培，字仲謙，江蘇無錫人。 道光二年舉人。 會試十三次不遇，考教習，補左翼宗學教習。 期滿，用知縣，咸豐元年，選授廣東從化縣。 時廣西賊起，廣州為賊出沒所，從化界連七邑，距府城百七十里。 四年，賊偪廣州，福培以花縣之石角及縣境之太平場為從化及諸邑屏障，請大府屯兵二千，兼可斷賊糧道，不報。 乃自募壯丁數百人，與典史趙應端及從弟性培分將之。 七月，賊數千直薄城下，福培登陴固守，率兵民力戰，凡七捷，斬八百餘級。 九月，援賊大至，急解縣印授其子送省會，而誓以死守。 賊舁砲攻城，裂數丈，賊蜂擁入。 與應端、性培等巷戰，身受數傷，退至學宮尊經閣，猶投石殪賊，賊焚閣，三人同死之。 僕週鏞、勇丁蘇兆英等皆殉難。 卹福培贈知府銜，建專祠，特諡剛烈。 福培就義處有血影漬地，如人形，濯之愈顯，後任建石欄護之，榜曰「忠跡昭然」。
Li Fupei, styled Zhongqian, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu. He passed the provincial examinations in the second year of Daoguang. After failing the metropolitan examination thirteen times, he qualified as an instructor and was appointed to the Left Wing Clan School. When his term expired he was appointed a county magistrate, and in the first year of Xianfeng was posted to Conghua in Guangdong. Bandits had risen in Guangxi, and Guangzhou was constantly raided. Conghua bordered seven districts and lay one hundred seventy li from the prefectural city. In the fourth year rebels pressed Guangzhou. Fupei argued that Shijiao in Huaxian and Taipingchang in his county were the shield for Conghua and neighboring districts, and asked the provincial government to post two thousand troops there to cut the enemy's supply line. He received no answer. He then recruited several hundred men on his own and divided command with Clerk Zhao Yingduan and his younger cousin Xingpei. In the seventh month several thousand rebels reached the walls. Fupei manned the battlements, led soldiers and townspeople in seven victories, and killed more than eight hundred enemy. In the ninth month a large relief force of rebels arrived. He hurriedly gave the county seal to his son to send to the provincial capital and swore to hold the city to the death. The rebels brought up cannon, blasted a breach several zhang wide, and poured in. He fought in the alleys with Yingduan, Xingpei, and others, taking many wounds. He fell back to the Zunjing Pavilion in the school compound and still threw stones, killing rebels. They burned the pavilion, and all three died together. His servant Zhou Yong, militiaman Su Zhaoying, and others died with him. Fupei was granted posthumous honors, the nominal rank of prefect, a dedicated shrine, and the special posthumous title Ganglie. Where Fupei died, a bloodstain shaped like a human figure grew clearer each time it was washed. A later official fenced it with stone and posted a tablet: "His Loyal Deeds Shine Forth."
27
王恩綬，字樂山，亦無錫人。 與福培為中表昆弟。 少以諸生受知巡撫林則徐，招入節署讀書，稱為篤行君子。 道光二十九年順天鄉試舉人，考充宗學教習，勤其職。 惠親王稽察宗學，語人曰：「不視此職為具文，孜孜不倦者，王教習一人而已。 」期滿，以知縣候選。 恩綬幼與福培同學，長以氣節相砥礪。 同居京師，夜分論時事，慷慨罵諸將吏棄城與軍，輒面發赤。 戟手搏案，聲震鄰舍，僮僕為驚起。 福培仕廣東，恩綬與之書曰：「大丈夫當此時，與其老死牖下，孰若埋骨疆場耶？ 」及福培殉，益躍躍欲得一當。
Wang Enshou, styled Leshan, was also from Wuxi. He and Fupei were cousins by marriage. As a young student he won favor with Governor Lin Zexu, who took him into his staff to study and called him a man of steadfast character. He passed the Shuntian provincial examinations in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, became an instructor in the Clan School, and served diligently. Prince Hui inspected the Clan School and said: "Of all who do not treat this post as empty formality, only Instructor Wang works tirelessly." When his term ended he was placed on the waiting list for a county magistracy. Enshou had studied with Fupei since childhood, and as adults they spurred each other to live by principle. They lived together in the capital and talked politics far into the night. Enshou would rage against generals and officials who abandoned cities and troops until his face flushed red. He would jab the table so hard the neighbors heard, and the servants would start awake. When Fupei went to Guangdong, Enshou wrote: "In times like these, is it better for a true man to die old at home or leave his bones on the battlefield?" After Fupei was killed, he grew ever more eager for his own chance to fight.
28
明年冬，武漢克復，當事以恩綬死事狀上聞，得旨賜祭葬，予諡武愍。 既而御史汪朝棨疏言：「恩綬無守土責，而視死如歸，不特與草間偷活判若天淵，即較之城亡與亡亦分難易。 且忠孝一門，僕從皆知赴戰，尤足扶植綱常。 請於本籍建專祠。 」會巡撫郭柏廕亦疏請建祠武昌，詔並許之。
The next winter, after Wuhan was recovered, officials reported Enshou's death in service. The throne granted sacrificial rites and burial honors and posthumously titled him Wumin. Then Censor Wang Chaoqi wrote: "Enshou had no duty to defend a district, yet he faced death as calmly as going home. That sets him not only far above those who cling to life in hiding, but even above officials who die when their cities fall." "Loyalty and filial piety filled one household, and even his servants rushed into battle—an example that upholds moral order." "I ask that a dedicated shrine be built in his home district." Governor Guo Baoxin also asked for a shrine at Wuchang, and the throne approved both requests.
29
李右文，字伯蘭，順天通州人。 舉人。 ，選授湖南東安知縣。 粵匪犯天津，留辦本籍團練，以功賞知州銜。 五年，赴官，值湘南道梗，諸弟馳書尼其行，不聽。 至楚，權新寧。 邑屢被寇，戶口流亡，右文招集撫循，凋敝以振。 七年，以最調祁陽，時從弟載文殉難廣西，弟复馳書勸歸，慨然曰：「死生命也，脫捐頂踵報國，是得死所也，何慮為！ 」尋回東安任。 八年，湖南境賊退，右文謂眾曰：「賊敗他竄，不可恃。 」亟訓練民團，置倉穀數千石，備不虞。
Li Youwen, styled Bolan, came from Tongzhou in Shuntian. He was a provincial graduate. He was appointed magistrate of Dong'an in Hunan. When Guangdong rebels threatened Tianjin, he stayed to organize home-district militia and was awarded the nominal rank of prefect for his service. In the fifth year he set out for his post. Roads in southern Hunan were blocked, and his brothers wrote urgently begging him not to go, but he refused. When he reached Hunan he served as acting magistrate of Xinning. The district had been raided repeatedly and the people had fled. Youwen gathered and comforted them until the ruined county revived. In the seventh year he was transferred to Qiyang for outstanding service. His cousin Zaiwen had just been killed in Guangxi, and his brothers again urged him to come home. He said: "Life and death are fate. If I can give even my body to the state, that is a worthy death—why should I fear?" He soon returned to his post at Dong'an. In the eighth year rebels withdrew from Hunan. Youwen told the people: "Defeated rebels simply move elsewhere—do not grow complacent." He hurriedly drilled the militia and stored several thousand piculs of grain against emergencies.
30
九年春，石達開由江西回竄湖南，逼近東安，新寧紳眾數百人來迎，請避賊新寧。 右文曰：「吾去，誰為守此土者？ 」已，復請護家口出境，又曰：「是為民望也。 」卻其請。 眾泣，誓死不忍去。 三月，賊麕至，城卑，四面皆山，賊環瞰之。 右文集城中官民登陴固守，親冒矢石，曆七晝夜，轟斃城下賊甚夥。 城陷，與賊巷戰署東，身被重創，猶手刃數賊，力竭遇害，賊燔其屍，僅得脊骨歸葬。 子傑、妻郝、子婦王，及僕婢，皆從死。 新寧紳眾數百，亦先後戰死。 詔視道員例賜卹，建祠本籍，隨殉親丁、紳勇附祀。
In the spring of the ninth year Shi Dakai fled from Jiangxi back into Hunan and approached Dong'an. Several hundred Xinning gentry came and urged him to take refuge in Xinning. Youwen said: "If I leave, who will defend this land?" They then asked him to send his family away, but he said: "That would destroy the people's hope." He refused. The people wept and vowed they would not abandon him. In the third month rebels swarmed in. The walls were low and mountains ringed the city on every side, so the enemy looked down from all around. Youwen gathered officials and townspeople on the walls. He braved arrows and stones himself. For seven days and nights cannon fire killed great numbers of rebels below the walls. When the city fell he fought in the alleys east of the yamen. Badly wounded, he still cut down several rebels before he was killed. The enemy burned his body; only his spine was recovered for burial. His son Jie, his wife Lady Hao, his daughter-in-law Lady Wang, and their servants all died with him. Several hundred Xinning gentry also fell in battle. An edict granted him posthumous honors at the level of a circuit intendant, ordered a shrine in his home district, and enshrined with him the kin, gentry, and militia who died with him.
31
子傑，字小蘭。 縣丞。 有幹略，侍父湖南，襄督練勇，進知縣。 方賊之回竄也，右文知不免，作書與諸弟訣，命傑齎往，意欲生之也。 傑不忍去，又重逆父命，潛避署左右，觀賊變。 賊至，率練勇守南門，城陷，聞警馳父所，未至，遇害，屍同被焚。 視同知例賜卹。
His son Jie, styled Xiaolan. He was an assistant magistrate. Capable and resolute, he accompanied his father in Hunan, helped direct the militia, and was promoted to county magistrate. When the rebels were returning, Youwen knew he would not survive. He wrote farewell letters to his brothers and sent Jie to deliver them, hoping to save his life. Jie could not bear to leave, yet he could not openly defy his father, so he hid near the yamen to watch events unfold. When the rebels came he led militia at the south gate. After the city fell he ran to his father at the first alarm, but was killed before he arrived; his body was burned too. He received posthumous honors at the level of a subprefect.
32
載文，字潞帆，右文從弟。 舉人。 三十年，以知縣發廣西，咸豐元年，權馬平縣。 時洪秀全犯桂林，馬平賊李志信響應，載文率兵剿捕，殲之。 尋調平南，五年，艇匪梁培友由梧州上竄，陷潯州，擾平南，載文御之渡口，砲轟沉其船，追擊斃匪無數。 賊屢分撲南北岸，悉卻之。 累以功擢同知直隸州。
Li Zaiwen, styled Lufan, was Youwen's younger cousin. He was a provincial graduate. In the thirtieth year he was posted to Guangxi as a county magistrate. In the first year of Xianfeng he acted as magistrate of Maping. When Hong Xiuquan attacked Guilin, the Maping bandit Li Zhixin rose in support. Zaiwen led troops against him and wiped him out. He was soon transferred to Pingnan. In the fifth year the river pirate Liang Peiyou came up from Wuzhou, seized Xunzhou, and raided Pingnan. Zaiwen met him at the crossing, sank his boats with cannon fire, and killed countless rebels in pursuit. The rebels repeatedly attacked both banks of the river; he beat them back each time. For repeated victories he was promoted to subprefect of Zhili.
33
六年五月至七月，賊麕至，水陸環攻，載文偕參將曾廷相、張遇清，都司唐文燦等，嬰城固守，困重圍七十餘日。 乞援、乞餉，告急文數十上，大吏但空言慰藉。 載文知事不可為，遣親僕間道以縣印檄送桂林，獨激勵兵勇與賊相持，教諭傅揚清，把總呂耀文，生員傅揚芬、吳國霖先後戰死。 賊攻益急，載文中砲傷腿，痛哭，北面頓首曰：「臣力盡，惟以一死報國，然不忍百姓屠戮也。 」縱之去。 千總方源開城私遁，賊乘隙入。 載文、廷相率勇巷戰，手刃數十賊，力竭，自剄不殊，賊擁至船中，抗罵不屈，並臠割之。
From the fifth to the seventh month of the sixth year, rebels swarmed in and attacked from land and sea, encircling the city. Zaiwen, together with Assistant Generals Zeng Tingxiang and Zhang Yuqing, Regional Commander Tang Wencan, and others, held the walls in a desperate defense and endured a siege of more than seventy days. They pleaded for relief troops and provisions and sent dozens of urgent dispatches, but the senior officials replied with nothing but hollow reassurance. Seeing that all was lost, Zaiwen sent a trusted servant by a back road to carry the county seal and official dispatches to Guilin, while he alone rallied the troops to keep fighting the rebels. Instructor Fu Yangqing, Platoon Commander Lü Yaowen, and the student scholars Fu Yangfen and Wu Guolin fell in battle one after another. As the rebel assault grew fiercer, Zaiwen was wounded in the leg by cannon fire. Weeping, he kowtowed toward the north and said, "I have spent my strength and can repay the dynasty only with my life — yet I cannot bear to see the people massacred." He then released the people and allowed them to leave. Company Commander Fang Yuan opened the gates and fled in secret, and the rebels poured in through the breach. Zaiwen and Tingxiang led their men in house-to-house fighting and personally killed dozens of rebels. When their strength failed they slit their own throats but did not die at once. The rebels dragged them onto a boat; they resisted and cursed without surrender, and were hacked to pieces.
34
是役也，遇清守北門，持大刀斫賊三十餘，被賊攢刺無完膚，死。 文燦守南城，率外委張珽巷戰死。 守備張彪守火藥局，燃火轟斃賊百餘，亦戰死。 載文、廷相死尤慘。 先是巡撫勞崇光奏薦載文堪勝道府，兵部侍郎王茂廕亦奏保循聲卓著，擢桂林遺缺知府。 命下，載文已遇害。 贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職，建祠本籍。 同治十年，追諡壯烈。
In that battle Yuqing held the north gate. Swinging a great sword he cut down more than thirty rebels, but they closed in and stabbed him until no whole patch of skin remained; he died. Wencan held the south gate and led Deputy Officer Zhang Cheng in street fighting until he was killed. Garrison Commander Zhang Biao defended the powder magazine, ignited it, and blew up more than a hundred rebels; he too died in the fight. The deaths of Zaiwen and Tingxiang were especially ghastly. Earlier Governor Luo Chongguang had recommended Zaiwen as qualified for a prefecture, and Vice Minister of War Wang Maoyin had likewise attested to his outstanding record of honest administration. He was promoted to fill the vacant prefecture of Guilin. By the time the appointment reached him, Zaiwen was already dead. He was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, awarded a hereditary office, and given a memorial shrine in his home district. In the tenth year of the Tongzhi reign he was posthumously given the title Zhuanglie, "Stout and Resolute."
35
李榞，字紫籓，安徽宣城人。 以監生入貲為知縣，，選授湖北公安，賑災有惠政。 調孝感，再調鍾祥。 咸豐二年，粵匪自長沙躪岳州，犯武昌，所在奸民競起，鍾祥馬騾子、襄陽郭大安、天門蓋天王皆盜魁，黨眾大者萬餘，小乃數千。 榞教練壯士千餘人，捕馬騾子及其黨數十人斬之。 偵知郭大安方謀以眾投粵賊，設伏間道擒之。 乘大霧掩擊蓋天王，悉俘其眾。 時武昌、漢陽相繼陷，上游諸郡帖然無恐者，榞平諸盜力也。 既而武昌复，大吏上榞功，擢荊門州知州，調署江夏縣，鍾祥民萬眾攀留不得。
Li Yuan, styled Zifan, was a native of Xuancheng in Anhui. By virtue of his status as an Imperial Academy student he bought appointment as county magistrate and was posted to Gong'an in Hubei, where his famine relief won the people's gratitude. He was transferred to Xiaogan and later to Zhongxiang. In the second year of Xianfeng the Taiping rebels swept from Changsha through Yuezhou against Wuchang, and local ruffians rose everywhere. Ma Luozi of Zhongxiang, Guo Da'an of Xiangyang, and Gai Tianwang of Tianmen were bandit chieftains whose followings ranged from several thousand to more than ten thousand. Yuan drilled more than a thousand strong men, captured Ma Luozi and dozens of his gang, and executed them. When he learned that Guo Da'an planned to defect with his men to the rebels, he laid an ambush on a side road and seized him. Under cover of thick fog he struck Gai Tianwang by surprise and took all his followers prisoner. Wuchang and Hanyang soon fell in turn, yet the upstream districts that stayed quiet and untroubled owed their peace to Yuan's suppression of the bandits. When Wuchang was recovered the provincial authorities reported Yuan's achievements; he was promoted to magistrate of Jingmen and assigned to act as magistrate of Jiangxia. Tens of thousands of people in Zhongxiang clung to him and would not let him go.
36
會粵匪林鳳祥等北犯，其後隊自河南折入湖北，陷黃梅，趨麻城。 榞率提標兵千人往援，擊賊黃岡之鵝公頸江口，大破之，窮追至安慶，與安慶兵夾擊，殲賊殆盡。 還值宿松警，复破賊下倉埠，詔以知府升用。 踰月，賊復自江西大至，寇廣濟之田家鎮，大吏檄榞往，連戰皆捷。 最後戰，他將懦不進，榞率所部渡江擊賊。 賊敗走，孤軍追賊，至興國州富池口，賊知榞軍無繼者，分舟中賊登岸襲其後。 榞引就水軍，水軍走左，陷淖中，與所部二百人皆鬥死，咸豐三年九月十日也。 事聞，贈道銜，予世職。 公安、鍾祥之民，家祭巷哭，奉木主祀之。
About then Lin Fengxiang's rebel column marched north while a rear detachment swung from Henan into Hubei, seized Huangmei, and advanced on Macheng. Yuan led a thousand provincial banner troops to their aid, routed the rebels at Egongjing on the Huanggang stretch of the Yangtze, pursued them to Anqing, and together with Anqing's garrison nearly wiped them out. On the way back he met an emergency at Susong and again defeated the rebels at Xiacangbu; an edict promoted him to prefect. A month later a large rebel force from Jiangxi struck Tianjia Town in Guangji. The authorities ordered Yuan to the front, and he won victory after victory. In the last engagement the other commanders hung back in fear; Yuan alone led his unit across the river to attack. The rebels broke and ran. Yuan pursued with his lone detachment as far as Fuchi Mouth in Xingguo Prefecture. Seeing that he had no support, the rebels sent men ashore from their boats to strike his rear. Yuan fell back toward the river fleet, but the sailors broke left and mired themselves in the mud; he and his two hundred men fought to the death on the tenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Xianfeng. When the report reached court he was posthumously granted the rank of circuit intendant and a hereditary office. The people of Gong'an and Zhongxiang mourned him in every home and alley, setting up spirit tablets to honor him.
37
始榞為縣，所至必於其地夷險豐耗、民俗醇訛、姦蠹根株、人所疾苦盡知之。 為治行之出於至誠，人樂為用，原效死力。 及其殉難，久而思之。 同治二年，湖北大吏復奏榞死事甚烈，在官政績尤著，請宣城及死事所建專祠，詔可，予諡剛介。
From his first posting as magistrate, Yuan made it his business to know each place thoroughly — its rugged and easy ground, its wealth and poverty, the decency or corruption of local custom, the roots of fraud, and every hardship the people suffered. Because he governed with complete sincerity, the people gladly followed him and were ready to die for him. Long after he gave his life, they still remembered him. In the second year of Tongzhi the Hubei authorities again reported that Yuan had died a hero's death and had an outstanding record in office, asking for special temples in Xuancheng and at the place of his death. The court agreed and granted him the posthumous title Gangjie, "Firm and Upright."
38
陳肖儀，字幼泉，江西弋陽人。 嘗遭母喪，扶柩舟行江中。 夜火發，四面皆烈焰，肖儀以身伏柩上，隨江流飄蕩，不死，柩亦無恙，一時稱奇孝。 年十九，官湖北縣丞，擢廣濟知縣。 咸豐三年，粵匪破田家鎮，去縣七十里，縣故無城垣，召募鄉兵，皆望風走。 肖儀知事不可為，持刃坐堂皇，賊入，數其罪，即抽刃自剄，未殊。 賊縛之，曳於市。 子恩藻奮臂擊賊，賊立殺之，肖儀罵益烈。 賊鑿齒刳頰，膚盡見骨，三日乃死，賊解其體為五。 縣民悲憤，賊去始斂焉。
Chen Xiaoyi, styled Youquan, was a native of Yiyang in Jiangxi. Once, while mourning his mother, he was escorting her coffin by boat on the river. One night fire broke out and flames closed in on every side. Xiaoyi threw himself over the coffin and drifted with the current; he survived, and the coffin was unharmed — an act people hailed at the time as miraculous filial devotion. At nineteen he served as an assistant magistrate in Hubei and was promoted to magistrate of Guangji. In the third year of Xianfeng the rebels overran Tianjia Town, seventy li from the county seat. The county had no walls. Xiaoyi tried to raise militia, but men fled at the mere rumor of the enemy. Knowing the cause was lost, Xiaoyi sat in the main hall with a blade in hand. When the rebels entered he denounced their crimes, then drew the blade and cut his throat, but did not die at once. The rebels bound him and dragged him through the streets. His son Enzao struck out at the rebels, who killed him on the spot. Xiaoyi cursed them all the more fiercely. The rebels knocked out his teeth and gouged his cheeks until the bone showed; after three days he died, and they cut his body into five parts. The county people were stricken with grief and rage; only after the rebels withdrew could they gather his remains.
39
萬成，滿洲鑲白旗人。 道光二十四年舉人，揀發湖北知縣，署漢川，調安陸。 咸豐四年，匪由武昌北竄，陷雲夢。 時總督台湧駐兵德安，萬成陳戰守二策，湧不能用，欲退守三關，徐圖克復，且諷與俱去。 萬成垂涕曰：「棄而不守，如百姓何​​？ 與城存亡，守土之義也！ 」其僕复勸之，並以主人無嗣為辭，萬成厲聲曰：「我家世受國恩，若臨難偷生，無以對國家，即無以對祖、父！ 」遂致書邑紳曰：「禍在旦夕，誰之責歟？ 一死塞責，不可為臣； 有辱於親，不可為子。 原不歸櫬於先人之墓，留葬於此，以志吾恨。 」是夜警報沓至，萬成召團練諸紳，告以在城兵勇俱隨總督北發，己當以死守城。 又知事必不濟，復作絕命書，與士民訣，略曰：「賊已至雲夢，勢必來德安，我惟攖城固守。 不能，則以死繼之。 諸君不我遐棄，能尋我遺骸，葬於碧霞台下，常此北望神京，則九原之下，感不忘矣！ 」逾日，賊距城二十餘裡，台湧擁兵徑去。 萬成謁知府議救急策，甫出署，紅巾賊數十突至。 知城陷，抽佩刀與戰，手刃數人，力竭死之，賊焚裂其屍。 德安复，縣民卒收葬殘骨於碧霞台下，以遂其志。
Wan Cheng was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner. A provincial graduate of the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, he was selected for a Hubei county magistracy, served as acting magistrate of Hanchuan, and was transferred to Anlu. In the fourth year of Xianfeng rebels fleeing north from Wuchang seized Yunmeng. Governor-General Tai Yong was then encamped at De'an. Wan Cheng offered plans for both attack and defense, but Tai Yong would not listen; he meant to withdraw to the Three Passes and recover the region slowly, and even hinted that Wan should leave with him. Wan Cheng wept and said, "If we abandon the city and refuse to defend it, what will become of the people?" "To stand or fall with the city — that is the obligation of the official who holds the land!" His servant urged him again, pleading that his master had no son. Wan Cheng said sternly, "My family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations. If I saved myself in this crisis I could not face the state — nor my ancestors and my father!" He then wrote to the local gentry: "Disaster hangs over us — upon whom does the blame fall?" "Only by dying can I answer for my duty; without that I am no fit servant of the throne." "To disgrace my parents — that I cannot do and still call myself a son." "I ask that my coffin not be returned to my ancestors' grave, but that I be buried here to mark my grief." That night warning after warning arrived. Wan Cheng called the militia gentry together and told them that every soldier in the city had marched north with the governor-general; he alone would hold the city to the death. Knowing defeat was certain, he wrote a final letter of farewell to officials and townspeople. It said in part: "The rebels have taken Yunmeng and will surely come to De'an. I shall cling to the walls and defend them to the end." "If I cannot hold them, I shall follow with my life." "If you do not forsake me in this distant post, and can find my body and bury it below Bixia Terrace so that I may forever face north toward the capital, then in the grave I shall never forget your kindness!" The next day the rebels were little more than twenty li away. Tai Yong marched off with his army without stopping. Wan Cheng went to the prefect to discuss emergency plans. The moment he stepped out of the yamen, dozens of red-turbaned rebels rushed upon him. Realizing the city was lost, he drew his side knife and fought, killing several men himself. When his strength failed he fell; the rebels burned and mutilated his body. After De'an was recovered the townspeople gathered his scattered bones and buried them below Bixia Terrace, as he had wished.
40
袁祖德，字又村，浙江錢塘人。 祖枚，以詩文名，官江寧，因家焉。 祖德早慧，入貲為江蘇寶山縣丞。 兵備道某稔其才，以上海縣令姚某漕事詿誤去，檄祖德擢縣事，且代姚辦漕，未五月，難作。 先是縣中團練多閩、廣無賴，本地遊民和之，漫無紀律。 粵匪據江寧為偽都，人心益搖，於是小刀會起事。 小刀會者，即無賴遊民所結合，黨羽散佈，官役皆為耳目。 道故粵產，謂中多粵人，置不為備； 先發難嘉定，戕縣官，道仍不為備。 咸豐三年八月初五日為上丁祀事日，黎明，祖德肅衣冠出，賊蟻擁入署。 一賊號小禁子者，祖德嘗因案懲之，首犯祖德，刃交於胸，被十餘創，罵不絕口，死。
Yuan Zude, styled Youcun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang. His grandfather Mei was famous for poetry and prose, served in Jiangning, and made his home there. Zude was gifted early. By purchased appointment he became assistant magistrate of Baoshan in Jiangsu. A defense circuit intendant who knew his ability, after Shanghai Magistrate Yao was removed over errors in the grain transport, ordered Zude promoted to run the county and to handle the transport in Yao's stead. Within five months rebellion broke out. The county militia had largely been drawn from Fujian and Guangdong ruffians, with local drifters joining in; there was no discipline at all. The rebels held Jiangning as their capital; morale wavered further, and then the Small Sword Society rose. The Small Sword Society was an alliance of idle ruffians whose agents were scattered everywhere; even yamen runners served as its spies. The circuit intendant was himself from Guangdong; seeing so many Cantonese among them, he took no precautions; They first rose in Jiading and killed the county magistrate, yet the intendant still made no preparations. On the fifth day of the eighth month of the third year of Xianfeng — the day of the shangding sacrifice — Zude came out at dawn in full official dress, and rebels poured into the yamen like ants. A rebel nicknamed Little Jingzi — whom Zude had once punished in court — was the first to strike him. Blades crossed at his chest; he took more than ten wounds, cursed without stopping, and died.
41
守備李大均得訊，躍馬呼殺賊，手無械，不能戰，自經死。
Garrison Commander Li Dajun heard the alarm, mounted his horse, and shouted to kill the rebels. With no weapon in hand he could not fight, and hanged himself.
42
於松，漢軍正黃旗人。 以廕授藍翎侍衛，出為江蘇松江糧廳。 春，南漕改海運，漕船水手將譁變，大吏檄松資遣，變遂定。 明年，大吏復以資遣事檄松，時粵賊已踞江寧為偽都，水手環而嘯呼，勢倍前。 松為上息內閧計，藉其精壯而訓練之，不旬日，得勁卒二千人。 會向榮躡賊圍江寧，江蘇境內稍安。 六年，率所籍卒從巡撫吉爾杭阿剿鎮江，既成營，搏賊銀山下，戰屢捷。 鎮江賊仰息江寧，既屢創，閉壘，潛略高資鎮。 松以千人馳擊，渡夾江，平賊營。 改攻鎮江城，以眾夜薄城下，梯垣縱火，潮勇噪而驚賊。 賊起，燃巨砲，登者紛墜。 松督隊在前，鉛丸中額，僕牙旗下，旋卒。 潮勇故剽椎名盜，居嘗啗賊金，故為賊用，敗官軍。 松死，麾下士千餘人，悲憤痛哭不忍聞。
Yu Song was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner. By hereditary privilege he entered service as a blue-plume imperial guardsman and later became grain intendant of Songjiang in Jiangsu. That spring the southern tribute grain was shifted to sea transport. The grain-boat sailors were near mutiny; the authorities ordered Song to arrange their dismissal and pay, and the trouble subsided. The next year the authorities again ordered Song to handle dismissals. By then the rebels held Jiangning; the sailors gathered, shouting and clamoring, in numbers twice those of the year before. Song sought to quell internal unrest for the court; he took the strongest among them and drilled them, and in less than ten days had two thousand seasoned troops. About then Xiang Rong was pressing the siege of Jiangning, and conditions in Jiangsu eased somewhat. In the sixth year he led the men he had enrolled and followed Governor Jirhanga against the rebels at Zhenjiang. Once the camp was set they fought below Silver Mountain and won repeated victories. The Zhenjiang rebels depended on Jiangning for support. After repeated defeats they closed their fortifications and secretly raided Gaozi Town. Song raced after them with a thousand men, crossed the Jiajiang, and overran the rebel camp. He then turned to assault Zhenjiang itself. At night he brought a large force up to the walls; his men scaled the ramparts and set fires, and the Chaoyong militia raised a din that startled the rebels. The rebels roused themselves, fired heavy cannon, and men on the ladders fell in droves. Song commanded from the front rank; a musket ball struck his forehead and he fell beneath his commander's banner, dying moments later. The Chaoyong militia were by nature notorious brawlers and bandits; they had often taken rebel bribes while garrisoned there, and the rebels used them to turn the battle against the government troops. When Song fell, more than a thousand of his men wept in grief and fury — the sound was almost unbearable.
43
尚那布，國羅落氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。 咸豐三年，由舉人揀發江蘇知縣，八年，署溧陽。 僕從蕭然，日集士紳議戰守，不退食。 兵勇踐境，親立城卡彈壓，出境乃已。 創義學，築舍數十楹，集諸生講肄，購田百餘畝供膏火。 修葺文廟，庀材鳩胥，捐廉為之倡。 疏濬城河，懋遷稱便。 迭以軍需籌防、催徵力最，賞知府銜。 十年賊陷廣德，溧陽界其北，尚那布誓死守。 賊眾逼城下，急切無援，督練勇擊賊退。 未幾，賊復大集，攻城愈迫，越日城陷。 尚那布厲聲叱曰：「我溧陽知縣，練勇殺賊，我作主，速殺我，勿傷百姓！ 」遂遇害。 卹贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職。 時署金壇縣知縣李淮同以城陷殉難。
Shangnabu, of the Guoluoluo clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner. A provincial graduate selected in the third year of Xianfeng for a Jiangsu county magistracy, he served as acting magistrate of Liyang in the eighth year. He kept few servants; each day he met with the gentry to discuss defense and ate at his post without leaving. When troops and militia trampled the countryside he personally stood at the city checkpoint to enforce order, and only withdrew once they had left the district. He founded a charity school, built several dozen rooms, gathered students for instruction, and bought more than a hundred mu of land to support their supplies and lamp oil. He restored the Confucian temple, gathered materials and labor, and led the effort with contributions from his own salary. He dredged the city moat, to the great convenience of local merchants. Again and again, for his exceptional work in army supplies, defense preparations, and tax collection, he was rewarded with the rank of prefect. In the tenth year the rebels captured Guangde. Liyang lay just to the north, and Shangnabu swore to hold the city to the last. The rebel army pressed against the walls. Relief was desperately needed, but none came. He rallied the trained militia, drove the attack, and forced the rebels back. Before long the rebels massed again. The siege tightened day by day, and the city fell the following morning. Shangnabu shouted in a thunderous voice: "I am the magistrate of Liyang! My militia kill rebels—I give the orders. Kill me at once, and do not touch the people! He was then put to death. He was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and awarded a hereditary office. At the same time Li Huai, acting magistrate of Jintan County, also died defending the city when it fell.
44
淮，字小石，浙江鄞縣人。 固守至百餘日，賊乘霧登城，淮朝服坐堂皇，罵賊死之。
Li Huai, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was from Yin County in Zhejiang. He held out for more than a hundred days. The rebels scaled the walls in a fog. Li Huai sat in full court dress in the yamen hall, cursed them to their faces, and was killed.
45
唐治，字魯泉，江蘇句容人。 道光五年舉人，大挑知縣，分安徽，補桐城縣。 歲大水，請帑勸分，按口賑施，不假手胥吏，一月鬚髮為白。 調祁門，舊有東山書院，生童膏火取給鹽釐，治別籌捐項充經費，士商兩便之。 又立義廒，積穀至數万石。 時粵賊據江寧，安徽改省治廬州，賊船上下無所忌。 上書陳利害，不報； 祁門無兵，依山為城，徽州以富名，賊欲圖徽，必道祁，請以兵守，又不報； 而祁之奸民前苦治嚴緝者，遂為賊鄉道。 道光四年正月，賊入縣屬櫸根嶺，治招集團丁，激以大義，誓共城存亡。 時大洪司巡檢鍾普塘亦帶勇入城協守，賊偪西門，治督眾登陴迎戰，砲轟斃匪數十人。 大股猝至，城遂陷，猶奮勇巷戰，力竭馬蹶，與普塘同時被執。 誘降不可，凌辱之，不屈，以禮遇之，終不食飲，卒罵賊死。 普塘同時遇害，沉屍於河。
Tang Zhi, courtesy name Luquan, was from Jurong in Jiangsu. A provincial graduate of the fifth year of Daoguang, he was selected in the secondary examination for a magistracy, assigned to Anhui, and posted to Tongcheng County. When a great flood struck, he petitioned for treasury grain and urged private contributions, distributing relief by head count himself without leaving the work to clerks. Within a month his hair had turned white. Transferred to Qimen, he found the old Dongshan Academy relying on salt surcharges for students' stipends. He raised separate donations to fund it instead, to the benefit of both scholars and merchants. He also established public granaries and stockpiled tens of thousands of shi of grain. The Cantonese rebels then held Nanjing. Anhui's provincial capital had been moved to Luzhou, and rebel boats moved freely up and down the rivers. He memorialized the throne on the strategic situation and received no answer; Qimen had no garrison. The town was built against the hills, and wealthy Huizhou lay beyond—the rebels would have to pass through Qimen to reach it. He asked for troops to hold the place and again received no answer; Local ruffians who had chafed under his strict policing now guided the rebels through the countryside. In the first month of the fourth year of Daoguang, rebels entered Jungen Ridge in the county. Tang Zhi rallied the militia, stirred them with appeals to duty, and swore to live or die with the city. Zhong Putang, patrol inspector of Dahong, also brought his braves into the city to help defend it. When the rebels pressed the west gate, Tang Zhi led the men to the walls and opened fire, killing dozens. A large rebel column arrived without warning and the city fell. He still fought house to house until his strength gave out and his horse went down. He and Putang were captured together. They tried to win him over, then humiliated him, but he would not break. When they treated him with courtesy instead, he still refused food and drink and at last cursed the rebels and died. Putang was killed at the same time, and their bodies were thrown into the river.
46
普塘，紹興人。 賊欲說降之，曰：「吾年逾六十矣，即不知羞恥事，能再活六十餘耶？ 」傳其罵賊尤烈雲。 ，曾國籓請於祁門建專祠，以鍾普塘附祀。
Putang was from Shaoxing. When the rebels tried to talk him into surrendering, he said: "I am already past sixty. Even if I were shameless enough to serve you, could I expect another sixty years of life? It is said that his curses against the rebels were fiercer still. Zeng Guofan petitioned for a dedicated shrine at Qimen, with Zhong Putang enshrined beside Tang Zhi.
47
賊躪安徽，守土吏殉節死者，又有泗州知州鄭沅，六安州知州金寶樹，蒙城縣知縣宋維屏，望江縣知縣衛君選，盱眙縣知縣許垣。 沅，順天大興人； 寶樹，江蘇元和人； 君選，河南趙城人； 垣，江蘇上元人； 維屏籍未詳。
As the rebels overran Anhui, other local officials who died holding their posts included Zheng Yuan, prefect of Sizhou; Jin Baoshu, prefect of Lu'an; Song Weiping, magistrate of Mengcheng; Wei Junxuan, magistrate of Wangjiang; and Xu Yuan, magistrate of Quanyang. Zheng Yuan was from Daxing in Shuntian; Jin Baoshu was from Yuanhe in Jiangsu; Wei Junxuan was from Zhaocheng in Henan; Xu Yuan was from Shangyuan in Jiangsu; Song Weiping's place of registration is not recorded.
48
林源恩，字秀三，四川達州人。 拔貢生。 舉順天鄉試，咸豐元年，選湖南平江縣知縣。 二年秋，粵賊犯長沙，瀏陽、通城匪徒皆為亂，三縣皆與平江接壤。 源恩詰姦守隘，如防禦水，截然不得蟄。 江忠源以為才，保奏知州銜​​，又以書播告士友，道「林某堪軍旅」也。 時曾國籓治兵長沙，檄源恩募平江勇五百人以從。 旋有他賊自崇陽、通城犯平江，檄源恩回援，壁北鄉之上塔市。 三月四日，賊大至，環源恩壘，源恩逆戰，大捷，追奔數十里。 既而塔齊布、胡林翼師克通城，平江解嚴，師別剿，則賊仍麕至，源恩屢戰卻之。 會有忌源恩者，功不得敘，又別摭他事中之。 源恩憤甚，詣大府自陳，而謇於辭，卒莫能自達。
Lin Yuan'en, courtesy name Xiusan, was from Dazhou in Sichuan. He was a selected tribute student. After passing the Shuntian provincial examination, he was appointed magistrate of Pingjiang County in Hunan in the first year of Xianfeng. In the autumn of the second year the Cantonese rebels attacked Changsha. Bandits in Liuyang and Tongcheng rose everywhere, and all three counties bordered Pingjiang. Yuan'en rooted out traitors and held the passes as tightly as one would hold back floodwater—not even a spy could slip through. Jiang Zhongyuan recognized his talent, recommended him for the rank of prefect, and wrote to fellow scholars that "Lin is fit for military service." At that time Zeng Guofan was drilling troops at Changsha and ordered Yuan'en to raise five hundred Pingjiang braves to join him. Soon other rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng attacked Pingjiang. Yuan'en was ordered back to relieve the county and encamped at Shangtashi in the north. On the fourth day of the third month the rebels arrived in force and surrounded his camp. Yuan'en met them head-on, won a great victory, and pursued the fleeing enemy for dozens of li. Then Taqibu and Hu Linyi captured Tongcheng and the emergency in Pingjiang ended. When the main army marched off on other campaigns, rebels still kept gathering, and Yuan'en beat them back again and again. Some who envied him saw that his merits went unrewarded, while others dredged up other charges against him. Yuan'en was furious. He went to the provincial capital to plead his own case, but he was halting in speech and could not make himself understood.
49
遂從國籓九江軍，命治羅澤南糧台。 乙卯春，從克廣信，賞花翎。 又治塔齊布糧台，旋任水師營務。 十一月，又攝理陸軍於廬山之麓、姑塘之南，而江西巡撫聞源恩賢，飛檄至南昌，付以所新募之平江營者。 源恩在廬山，又與共事武夫不相能，憤彌甚，嘗獨歎曰：「丈夫一死強寇耳，終不返顧矣！ 」
He then joined Zeng Guofan's army at Jiujiang and was put in charge of Luo Zinan's supply depot. In the spring of the yimao year he took part in the capture of Guangxin and was awarded the peacock feather. He also managed Taqibu's supply depot and soon took charge of the naval camp. In the eleventh month he also took acting command of the army at the foot of Mount Lu, south of Guta. Meanwhile the Jiangxi governor, hearing of Yuan'en's ability, sent urgent orders to Nanchang placing the newly raised Pingjiang battalion under his command. At Mount Lu Yuan'en again could not work with the rough soldiers around him, and his anger only deepened. Once he sighed alone: "A true man need only die fighting fierce rebels—then he will never look back! "
50
明年，石達開犯江西，連陷八府五十餘州縣。 六年三月，李元度率師自湖口南來，源恩與鄧輔綸自南昌而東，兩軍會於撫州，克進賢東鄉，進破文昌橋堅壘五，赭其巢。 既薄城，源恩壁南門，元度壁西南隅，相去四里。 賊嬰城拒守，堅不可拔。 當是時，江、楚道梗，瑞、臨、袁、吉四郡無一官軍。 援賊不時至，​​至則合城賊來犯，所部迎擊三十里外，輒重創之，破賊壘者九，大小戰五十有六，皆告捷。 然部下血戰久，疲不得休，裹創者十之三，病者十四五。 會輔綸中蜚語去，在事者多告退，源恩勢益孤，餉日絀。
The next year Shi Dakai invaded Jiangxi and in succession overran more than fifty prefectures and counties across eight circuits. In the third month of the sixth year Li Yuandu led his army south from Hukou while Yuan'en and Deng Fulun marched east from Nanchang. The two forces met at Fuzhou, took Jinxian and Dongxiang, broke five strongholds at Wenchang Bridge, and burned the rebel camps. When they drew near the city, Yuan'en encamped at the south gate and Yuandu at the southwest corner, four li apart. The rebels held the city and resisted stubbornly; it could not be taken by assault. At that time the routes between the Yangtze and Chu were cut off, and not a single government army remained in the four prefectures of Rui, Lin, Yuan, and Ji. Rebel reinforcements arrived at irregular intervals. Whenever they came they joined the garrison in attacking, and his troops met them thirty li outside the city and repeatedly inflicted heavy losses. They broke nine rebel camps and fought fifty-six engagements, large and small, all reported as victories. Yet his men had fought bloody battles for so long that they could not rest. One in three was bandaged for wounds, and fourteen or fifteen in a hundred were sick. Then Fulun left under a cloud of slander, many on the staff resigned, Yuan'en's position grew ever more isolated, and supplies ran short day by day.
51
宜黃、崇仁兩縣來乞師，謂克宜、崇則能拊撫賊之背，且勸士民輸餉，可得十數万。 源恩與元度遂分江、楚軍共五千徇西路。 九月三日，克宜黃，九日，克崇仁，俘斬各數百。 忽皖賊數千自景德鎮來援，急撤宜、崇軍，官民苦留不遣。 將士亦以久飢甫得一飽，不能行。 賊趨撫州，十六日，扼河而戰。 水涸，賊駷馬飛渡，追而敗諸城下。
Officials from Yihuang and Chongren came begging for troops, saying that if those counties were taken the army could strike the rebels from behind and persuade the gentry and people to deliver supplies worth one or two hundred thousand taels. Yuan'en and Yuandu then split off five thousand Jiang-Chu troops and marched along the western route. On the third day of the ninth month they took Yihuang, and on the ninth they took Chongren, capturing and killing several hundred rebels in each place. Suddenly several thousand Anhui rebels came from Jingdezhen to reinforce the enemy. They hurriedly withdrew from Yihuang and Chongren, though officials and people begged them desperately to stay. The troops too, long starving and having just eaten their first full meal in days, could not march. The rebels rushed toward Fuzhou, and on the sixteenth they gave battle at a river crossing. The river had run dry, and rebel horses galloped across. They pursued and defeated the enemy below the city.
52
先是源恩所部之右護軍遣赴崇仁，留三百人守壘，賊诇知之，詰旦出犯，先陷右軍，遂圍源恩壁。 源恩慷慨諭將士曰：「好男子，努力殺賊，無走也！ 」眾皆應曰：「惟公命。 」都司唐德昇馳入壁，掖源恩上馬，源恩曰：「此吾死所也，子受事日淺，其行乎！ 」德昇曰：「君能死，吾獨不能死耶？ 」從容解金條脫畀其從子某，曰：「若馳去，吾與林公死此矣！ 」壘破，源恩手劍鏦賊，力竭，死之。 德昇素驍健，格殺十餘賊，始被害。 從死者三百餘人。 源恩年僅四十。 追贈道員，賜卹如例。
Earlier Yuan'en had sent his Right Guard Corps to Chongren, leaving only three hundred men to hold the camp. The rebels learned this through spies. At dawn they attacked, first overrunning the right corps, then surrounding Yuan'en's camp. Yuan'en addressed his officers and men with passion: "Good men, fight hard and kill the rebels—do not run! The men all answered: "We obey your command alone. Battalion Commander Tang Desheng galloped into the camp and tried to lift Yuan'en onto a horse. Yuan'en said: "This is where I die. You have served only a short while—go! Desheng said: "If you can die, why should I alone not die? Calmly he removed a gold ingot and gave it to a nephew, saying: "Ride off quickly—I and Superintendent Lin will die here! The camp was overrun. Yuan'en fought hand to hand with his sword and killed rebels until his strength gave out and he fell. Desheng was by nature a fierce fighter. He killed more than ten rebels in close combat before he too was slain. More than three hundred died with them. Yuan'en was only forty years old. He was posthumously promoted to circuit intendant and granted the usual posthumous honors.
53
德昇，字彥遠，寧遠人。 舊隸副將周鳳山部下，以十五日奉檄來軍，十七日及難，贈游擊。
Tang Desheng, courtesy name Yanyuan, was from Ningyuan. He had formerly served under Deputy Commander Zhou Fengshan. On the fifteenth he received orders to join the army; on the seventeenth he met his death. He was posthumously promoted to battalion commander.
54
畢大鈺，湖南長沙人。 ，以附生守長沙南關，粵賊砲轟城塌，大鈺斂空棺實土為牆，頃刻成三十餘丈。 隨提督鄧紹良堅拒八十餘日，殲賊數千。 賊自湖北迴竄，湘潭、靖港均陷，大鈺復以防省功選用府經歷、縣丞。 湖北崇陽、通城陷，大鈺复領兵赴剿。 諜知賊由平江搗長沙，絕饋道，厲兵為備，賊不得逞。 行軍禁騷擾，一蔬一木無妄取。 通城亂久無官，為立團防，鋤土匪，通人安業。 因其歸，報金巨萬，大鈺卻不受。 四年，保用知縣，授浙江仙居知縣，案無留牘。 地瘠民貧，逋賦多，大鈺在官，民爭輸納。 尋捐知府，浙江巡撫何桂清留筦糧台，檄赴於潛防堵。 又以開化疊警，調防婺源。 初戰屢捷，尋賊以三千人圍南關，大鈺偕胞侄候選通判榮清合剿，賊大至，力竭，均死之。 卹贈太僕寺卿，賞世職。
Bi Dayu was from Changsha in Hunan. As a licensed student he helped defend Changsha's south gate. When Cantonese rebels blasted the wall until it collapsed, Dayu filled empty coffins with earth to build a rampart, and in moments thirty-odd zhang of wall were restored. He then served under Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang and held out for more than eighty days, destroying several thousand rebels. When the rebels doubled back from Hubei and Xiangtan and Jinggang both fell, Dayu was again selected for provincial office for his defense merits, as prefectural registrar and assistant magistrate. When Chongyang and Tongcheng in Hubei fell, Dayu again led troops to suppress the rebels. Intelligence showed the rebels would strike Changsha through Pingjiang and cut the supply lines. He hardened his troops in readiness, and the rebels could not succeed. On campaign he forbade looting; not a vegetable or branch was taken without cause. Tongcheng had long been in chaos without an official. He established militia defenses, uprooted local bandits, and the people of Tongcheng could return to their livelihoods. Grateful for the peace he had brought, the people offered him tens of thousands in gold, but Dayu refused. In the fourth year he was recommended for a magistracy and appointed magistrate of Xianju in Zhejiang, where no case files piled up on his desk. The land was poor and the people were impoverished, with heavy tax arrears. While Dayu held office, the people competed to pay their taxes. Soon he purchased the rank of prefect. The Zhejiang governor He Guiqing kept him to manage the grain depot and ordered him to Yuqian to block the enemy's advance. When Kaifeng raised repeated alarms, he was transferred to defend Wuyuan. At first he won repeated victories. Then three thousand rebels besieged the south gate. Dayu and his cousin, the candidate subprefect Rong Qing, counterattacked together, but the rebels came in force. Their strength gave out and both were killed. He was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and awarded a hereditary office.
55
湯世銓，字彥聲，順天大興籍，江蘇武進人。 舉人。 ，以知縣發浙江，七年，署開化縣。 時粵匪闌入浙境，由常山窺開化，委署者多不肯往，世銓獨毅然請行，至則募勇防守。 八年三月，賊首石達開擾浙，衢州鎮總兵饒廷選戰敗，遂偪開化。 世銓聞警登陴，賊突至，城陷，世銓拔佩刀自剄，為紳民奪刀擁出，不得死。 陰約各都結團，且飛書請兵，會鶴麗鎮總兵週天孚督軍追擊，賊奔處州，世銓率團沿途截殺。
Tang Shiquan, courtesy name Yansheng, was registered in Daxing, Shuntian, and was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu. He was a provincial graduate. Assigned to Zhejiang as a magistrate, in the seventh year he served as acting magistrate of Kaifeng County. Cantonese rebels had intruded into Zhejiang and were probing Kaifeng from Changshan. Many acting appointees refused to go, but Shiquan alone volunteered resolutely. Upon arrival he raised braves for the defense. In the third month of the eighth year the rebel leader Shi Dakai raided Zhejiang. Rao Tingxuan, regional commander at Quzhou, was defeated and the rebels then pressed toward Kaifeng. Shiquan heard the alarm and mounted the walls. The rebels burst in and the city fell. He drew his dagger to cut his throat, but gentry and commoners seized the blade and carried him out, so he could not die. He secretly arranged for each district to form militia companies and sent urgent dispatches requesting reinforcements. At the same time Zhou Tianfu, regional commander of Heli Town, led troops in pursuit; the rebels fled toward Chuzhou, and Shiquan led the companies to intercept and cut them down along the way.
56
六月，縣城复，仍因失守褫職，代未至，仍帶勇守禦。 七月，賊由常山復攻開化，江蘇候補知縣劉福林帥鄉勇方檄赴寧國。 世銓請於大府，留籍防禦，而以城守囑縣丞某，且出印印其衣，畢，遣人賚印至府授代者，遂出禦賊於華埠。 賊至，疊擊敗之。 會貴州定遠協副將硃貴統兵三千夾援，戰失利，世銓急整隊出，倉猝不能成陣，力鬥，與福林同歿於戰所。 以印衣覓得屍，胸腹腰肋創十數。 勇目方忠同死於其側。 事聞，復原官，卹如例，給世職。
In the sixth month the county seat was recovered. He was still stripped of office for having lost it, but his replacement had not yet arrived, so he continued to lead the braves in defense. In the seventh month the rebels again attacked Kaifeng by way of Changshan. Liu Fulin, a Jiangsu expectant magistrate, was leading local militia and had just received orders to proceed to Ningguo. Shiquan petitioned the provincial authorities to remain for local defense, entrusted the city’s defense to a certain assistant magistrate, and stamped his official seal on his garment. When that was done, he sent someone bearing the seal to the prefecture for his successor, then went out to engage the rebels at Huabu. When the rebels arrived, he struck them again and again and drove them off. Then Zhu Gui, vice commander of the Dingyuan Brigade in Guizhou, arrived with three thousand men in flanking support, but the battle went badly. Shiquan hastily assembled his troops and rushed out; in the confusion he could not form ranks. He fought with all his strength and fell on the field together with Fulin. They found his corpse by the stamped garment. His chest, belly, waist, and ribs bore more than ten wounds. The brave squad leader Fang Zhong also died at his side. When the matter was reported, his original office was restored, condolences were granted according to regulation, and a hereditary title was awarded.
57
謝子澄，字云航，四川新都人。 舉人，大挑知縣，分直隸。 咸豐元年，署無極縣，二年，補天津。 天津地濱海，獷悍難治，市有所謂「混混」者，健武善鬥。 子澄至，見前令系諸混混，歎曰：「是奚不可化者？ 」籍其名，縱之。 未幾，縱者閧於市，子澄按名捕，殛其魁，地面遂靖。 時粵匪出擾湘、漢，順流而東，遣酋林鳳祥、李開芳分兵渡河，莫測所向。 人方謂南北道隔，賊不敢犯，子澄深以為憂。 捐金倡團練，召所縱諸混混，以周處故事喻之，眾皆為用。 回民劉繼德复集回民千餘人應之，遂率赴教場，授器械，教戰陣之法，其妻亦撤簪珥以助。 長蘆鹽政文謙歸財與糧，隨時協濟，子澄得一意練兵。
Xie Zicheng, courtesy name Yunhang, was a native of Xindu in Sichuan. He was a provincial graduate, selected in the great promotion for magistrate, and assigned to Zhili. In the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Wuji County; in the second year he was appointed magistrate of Tianjin. Tianjin lies on the coast, and its people are fierce and hard to govern. In the marketplace there were men called "hunhun"—stout fellows skilled at fighting. When Zicheng arrived, he saw that the previous magistrate had imprisoned the various hunhun. He sighed and said, "Are these men beyond reform? " He registered their names and released them. Before long the released men raised a riot in the market. Zicheng arrested them by name, executed their ringleader, and the district was soon pacified. At that time Cantonese rebels were raiding Hunan and Hubei and sweeping downstream to the east. They sent chiefs Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang to divide their forces and cross the river, and no one could tell where they would strike next. People were saying that the routes north and south were cut off and the rebels would not dare invade, but Zicheng was deeply worried. He donated money to promote militia training, summoned the hunhun he had released, and used the story of Zhou Chu as a parable. They all answered his call. The Muslim Liu Jide also gathered more than a thousand fellow Muslims in response. Zicheng then led them to the drill ground, issued weapons, and taught them battle formations, and his wife removed her hairpins and earrings to contribute as well. Wenqian, the Changlu salt commissioner, returned funds and grain and assisted whenever needed, so Zicheng could devote himself entirely to drilling troops.
58
未幾，賊圍懷慶。 踰月，渡臨洺關，總督納爾經額帥師遁，遂經順河、柏鄉、欒城入深州。 主閫者務持重，雖數奉詔夾剿，而習於潰逃，數避賊。 其奮勇者尾追數千里，氣亦餒，賊勢益橫。 又經獻縣、交河，以薄滄州，滄州號有備，亦為所拔。 津地大震。
Before long the rebels besieged Huaqing. After more than a month they crossed Linming Pass. Governor-General Na'erjing'e led his army in flight, and the rebels passed through Sunhe, Baixiang, and Luancheng and entered Shenzhou. The commanders-in-chief prized caution. Though repeatedly ordered to attack the rebels from both sides, they were accustomed to breaking and fleeing and repeatedly avoided them. Those who fought bravely pursued them for thousands of li, but their spirit flagged as well, and the rebels grew ever more rampant. They passed through Xian County and Jiaohe and pressed toward Cangzhou. Cangzhou was said to be well prepared, yet it too was taken. Tianjin was greatly shaken.
59
九月，賊至梢直口，大吏不知所為，議嬰城守。 子澄以負郭居民數十萬，不應棄之，力爭。 遂用沿河棹小舟以火器取野鶩者，又火會會眾萬人，合水陸拒賊，而別向火會首事張錦文籌貲。 先是錦文輸家財濬壕，壕成，運河水大至，環城窪下成巨浸，而葡萄窪尤甚。 子澄阻壕守，渡壕擊賊。 賊酋開山王小禿子手黃旗指揮，迅奮剽疾，能一躍丈餘，避槍擊。 子澄先伏打野鴨船於岸外，賊以為民船也，呼渡，船槍發，殪小禿子，群賊奪氣。 伏舟進擊餘賊，血流染波。 日晡，軍餒，錦文又齎糗糧至，戰益奮。 勇目余鵬龍等相繼陷陣，复斬級無算，賊遁。 是役也，子澄功最，旨以知府用，留本任。
In the ninth month the rebels reached Shaozhikou. The high officials did not know what to do and discussed closing the city and holding out behind its walls. Zicheng argued that hundreds of thousands of residents outside the walls should not be abandoned and fought the proposal vigorously. They employed small boats that poled along the river and used firearms to hunt wild ducks, rallied ten thousand members of the Fire Association, combined land and water forces to resist the rebels, and separately sought funds from Zhang Jinwen, chief of the Fire Association. Earlier Jinwen had contributed his family wealth to dig moats. When the moats were finished, canal water surged in, the low ground around the city became a great flood, and Grape Hollow was deepest of all. Zicheng defended behind the moat and crossed it to strike the rebels. The rebel chief Little Baldy, King of Opening Mountains, commanded with a yellow flag in hand. Swift, fierce, and agile, he could leap more than a zhang and dodge gunfire. Zicheng had hidden duck-hunting boats offshore. The rebels took them for civilian craft and called to be ferried across; the boats opened fire and killed Little Baldy, and the rebels lost their nerve. The hidden boats advanced against the remaining rebels, and blood stained the waves. At dusk the army was hungry, but Jinwen arrived with dry rations and the fighting grew fiercer. The brave squad leaders Yu Penglong and others fell one after another in battle, but they cut countless enemy heads and the rebels fled. In this campaign Zicheng's merit was greatest. An edict appointed him for use as prefect while retaining his current post.
60
時賊退踞靜海及獨流鎮，子澄奉調赴勝保營，列營河西。 賊由獨流出撲，屢擊退之。 嗣靜海賊傾巢出援，子澄追剿，賊竄，正窘，會都統佟鑑思絕賊歸路，進掣壕板，以路滑失足踣地，賊刃交下。 子澄單騎馳救，砲洞馬腹，身受七傷。 鵬龍負之趨，子澄曰：「憊矣！ 爾亟行，毋顧我。 」賊酋高剛頭薄之急，子澄恐為所辱，沉於河。 鵬龍率從子陳樑等皆戰死。 事聞，加布政使銜，諡忠愍，建專祠。 喪車還津，無貴賤皆往吊，哭如私親。 天津祠落成，蠡縣人李某，生致高剛頭，剖心以祭。
At that time the rebels had fallen back to Jinghai and Duliuzhen. Zicheng was ordered to Sheng Bao's camp and encamped west of the river. The rebels sallied from Duliuzhen again and again, and he drove them back each time. Later the Jinghai rebels poured out in full force, and Zicheng pursued them. The rebels scattered in flight and were hard pressed when Commandant-in-chief Tong Jian tried to cut off their retreat, advanced to pull up the moat planks, slipped on the wet road and fell, and blades fell on him from all sides. Zicheng raced alone to rescue him. A cannonball pierced his horse's belly, and he himself took seven wounds. Penglong carried him in flight. Zicheng said, "I'm spent! Go at once—do not mind me. " The rebel chief Gaogang pressed close. Fearing disgrace at their hands, Zicheng drowned himself in the river. Penglong, together with his nephew Chen Liang and others, all died fighting. When the matter was reported, he was granted the rank of provincial administration commissioner, posthumously titled Zhongmin, and given a private shrine. When the funeral procession returned to Tianjin, nobles and commoners alike came to mourn, weeping as for a kinsman. When the Tianjin shrine was completed, a certain Li from Lixian captured Gaogang alive and cut out his heart as an offering.
61
子澄好為小詩，工駢體文，為政有聲，卒以殺賊致殞。 人謂賊自河北經山西，所至席捲無堅城，獨受挫於子澄，使京師得以為備，其關係尤重雲。
Zicheng enjoyed writing short poems and excelled at parallel prose. His governance was widely praised, and he died at last in the act of slaying rebels. People said that from Hebei through Shanxi the rebels swept all before them without meeting a strong city, and only at Zicheng were they checked, giving the capital time to prepare—a consequence of the greatest weight indeed.
62
先是賊過臨洺關，同知周憲曾公服坐餉鞘上，罵賊死。 後子澄以知縣死直隸者：江安瀾，廣西臨桂人。 舉人，挑教職，保知縣，發直隸，補柏鄉。 咸豐元年，調靜海。 賊北犯，靜海為畿南衝要，大軍援剿，供應無乏。 賊入境，偕署都司潘宗得等擒斬偽司馬陳得旺，大隊麕至，官軍眾寡不敵，遽潰。 城陷，赴水死。 破沙河，王衡身中七刃死； 破欒城，唐盛朝服罵賊，賊縛之柱上死，典史陳虎臣從死。
Earlier, when the rebels passed Linming Pass, Subprefect Zhou Xian sat in official dress on the silver convoy and cursed them until they killed him. Later, among the magistrates who died in Zhili like Zicheng was Jiang Anlan, a native of Lingui in Guangxi. He was a provincial graduate, selected for educational posts, recommended as magistrate, assigned to Zhili, and appointed to Baixiang. In the first year of Xianfeng he was transferred to Jinghai. When the rebels invaded from the north, Jinghai was a critical choke point south of the capital. Imperial armies came to aid in the suppression, and supplies never ran short. When the rebels entered the district, he and Acting Brigade Commander Pan Zongde and others captured and executed the false Sima Chen Dewang. A large rebel force then swarmed in; the government troops were outnumbered and suddenly broke. The city fell, and he drowned himself. When Shahe fell, Wang Heng took seven blade wounds and died; When Luancheng fell, Tang Sheng in official robes cursed the rebels; they bound him to a pillar and killed him, and Registrar Chen Huchen died with him.
63
又馬雲嵐，慶雲人。 州判。 賊犯縣城，率鄉團出禦，被執，不屈死。 子龍文從死。 卹如例，予世職。
There was also Ma Yunlan, a native of Qingyun. He was an assistant prefect. When the rebels attacked the county seat he led local militia out to resist. He was captured, refused to yield, and died. His son Longwen died with him. Condolences were granted according to regulation, and a hereditary title was awarded.
64
文穎，字魯齋，趙氏，漢軍正藍旗人。 進士，用知縣，發山東，補蒙陰。 邑患蝗，兩以文籥神，皆應。 調陽信，弭抗漕釁。 又調商河，濬徒駭河，境免積潦。 時粵匪已竄直隸之建通鎮，去商河百里，募練鄉勇，民恃無恐。 調省主糧台事，適股匪入東境，金鄉、鄆城皆陷，而陽穀當其衝。 大吏以文穎有幹才，檄令往署，至則城備久弛，急號召鄉團為守禦計。 是時將軍善祿擁重兵駐東昌，飛牒請援，置不應。 憤極，抵案曰：「死耳，復何言！ 」或諷以出城待援者，怒斥曰：「與城俱存亡，豈有臨難苟免之文某哉？ 」
Wen Ying, courtesy name Luqi, of the Zhao clan, was a Han Chinese Bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner. A jinshi, he was appointed magistrate, assigned to Shandong, and posted to Mengyin. When the county suffered locusts, he twice wrote petitions to the gods, and both times they were answered. Transferred to Yangxin, he quelled resistance to the grain transport. Transferred again to Shanghe, he dredged the Tuhai River and spared the district from accumulated flooding. At that time Cantonese rebels had fled to Jiantong Town in Zhili, a hundred li from Shanghe. He raised and drilled local militia, and the people relied on this and were unafraid. He was transferred to the province to manage the grain bureau. Just then roving bandits entered the eastern border; Jinxian and Yuncheng both fell, and Yanggu lay directly in their path. Knowing Wen Ying's ability, the high officials ordered him to go and act there. Upon arrival he found the city's defenses long neglected and urgently summoned local militia to plan its defense. At that time General Shanlu held heavy troops stationed at Dongchang. Urgent dispatches requesting aid were sent, but he ignored them. Furious beyond measure, he slammed the desk and said, "Death—that is all! What more is there to say! " When someone suggested leaving the city to await relief, he angrily rebuked them: "Live and die with the city—would a man named Wen flee in a crisis? "
65
未幾，賊大至，割半袖付僕馳報父母，即懷印上城，與典史徐鳳喈從容出印相視。 賊入城，怒馬馳入賊隊，被七創，罵不絕口死。 鳳喈及教官李文綬同遇害。 文穎抵任才五日，時咸豐四年二月二十九日。 事聞，優恤，立專祠，予世職。 文穎嘗過泰山，題句有云：「此行不了封侯業，原把頑軀竊比君。 」蓋以泰山自矢，見危授命，其志素定雲。 子四，三爾豐，自有傳。
Before long the rebels came in force. He cut off half a sleeve for a servant to rush word to his parents, then bearing the seal mounted the wall and calmly took out the seal with Registrar Xu Fengjie to look at it together. When the rebels entered the city he galloped his horse in fury into their ranks, took seven wounds, and cursed without cease until he died. Fengjie and Instructor Li Wenshou were also killed. Wen Ying had been in office only five days. It was the twenty-ninth day of the second month in the fourth year of Xianfeng. When the matter was reported, exceptional condolences were granted, a private shrine was built, and a hereditary title was awarded. Wen Ying once passed Mount Tai and inscribed a line: "On this journey I shall not finish the work of winning a marquisate; I would offer my stubborn frame in humble comparison to you. " He had taken Mount Tai as his vow; meeting peril he gave his life—his resolve had long been fixed indeed. He had four sons; the third, Erfeng, has his own biography.
66
張積功，江蘇儀徵人。 舉人。 大挑知縣，發山東，歷州縣吏。 二十年，初權臨淄。 前政不善，多流亡，以誠招徠之，皆歸故業。 即墨饑民滋擾，檄往辦理而定。 朝城民變，民聞積功治臨淄事，即首行館請死，喻以理，懲以法，皆歡呼去。 咸豐四年三月，賊攻臨清州，積功適知州事，守禦十四晝夜。 十四日，城陷，闔門死難。 初，賊過冠縣，知縣傅士珍自經死。
Zhang Jigong was a native of Yizheng in Jiangsu. He was a provincial graduate. Selected in the great promotion for magistrate, he was assigned to Shandong and served in various prefectural and county posts. In the twentieth year he first served as acting magistrate of Linzi. The previous administration had been poor and many had fled, but he recalled them with sincerity and all returned to their former occupations. Starving people in Jimo grew restless; he was ordered there to handle the matter and settled it. The people of Chaocheng rose in revolt. Hearing of Jigong's handling of affairs in Linzi, they went at once to the guesthouse and begged to die. He reasoned with them and punished by law, and all cheered and departed. In the third month of the fourth year of Xianfeng the rebels attacked Linqing Prefecture. Jigong happened to be acting prefect and defended for fourteen days and nights. On the fourteenth day the city fell, and his whole household died in the calamity. Earlier, when the rebels passed Guan County, Magistrate Fu Shizhen hanged himself.
67
典史瞿濬，字菊坪，江蘇武進人。 帥鄉勇出敵，遇賊城闉，中鳥槍，洞其肋，墜馬。 欲退保於司獄，賊追及，刃倳其胸，罵不絕口，剖腹死之。 妻呂氏，罵賊，被寸磔。 亦全家遇害，時三月朔也。
Registrar Qu Jun, courtesy name Juping, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu. He led local militia out to engage the enemy and met the rebels at the city gate. He was hit by a musket shot that pierced his ribs, and he fell from his horse. He tried to fall back and hold the prison office, but the rebels caught up, hacked his chest with blades, and disemboweled him as he cursed without cease. His wife, née Lü, cursed the rebels and was subjected to lingchi. His whole family was also killed. It was the first day of the third month.
68
冒芬，江蘇如皋人。 巡檢，發廣東，補北寨司巡檢，調五斗口。 緝獲盜匪傅敏南、烏石姊等，有能名。 擢廣州府經歷，調海豐縣丞。 英吉利擾廣州，以守城功進知縣，授開平縣。 縣介新會、鶴山間，盜賊出沒，芬嚴為條約，捕甚多。 歷權高要、曲江、乳源等縣。
Mao Fen was a native of Rugao in Jiangsu. He served as an inspector, was assigned to Guangdong, appointed inspector of the Beizhai station, and was transferred to Wudoukou. He apprehended the bandits Fu Minnan, Wushi Jie, and others, winning a reputation for ability. He was promoted to registrar of Guangzhou Prefecture and transferred to assistant magistrate of Haifeng County. When the English harassed Guangzhou, he was advanced to magistrate for merit in defending the city and appointed to Kaiping County. The county lay between Xinhui and Heshan, where bandits came and went. Fen established strict regulations and captured a great many of them. He successively served as acting magistrate of Gaoyao, Qujiang, Ruyuan, and other counties.
69
餘匪吳煥中、黃老滿等潛聚曲江龍歸墟，結連羅鏡墟凌十八，圖复逞。 煥中潛至乳源，為邏者獲。 芬訊得實，偕千總張鷹揚馳往，捕獲黃老​​滿等頭目十三名，解經曲江寺前村，猝與羅鏡賊遇。 鷹揚所部潰散，芬率親軍百餘人與賊戰，軍火盡，芬被創，賊奪黃老滿去。 芬裹創為書，上總督葉名琛，極言兩粵賊勢急，宜聯絡官民，早繕備具。 越數日，傷劇卒。 卹如例，後建專祠。
Remaining bandits Wu Huanzhong, Huang Laoman, and others secretly gathered at Longgui market in Qujiang and linked with Ling Shiba of Luojing market, plotting to rise again. Huanzhong secretly reached Ruyuan and was captured by border scouts. Fen interrogated the prisoners and confirmed the facts. Together with battalion commander Zhang Yingyang he rushed there and captured thirteen ringleaders including Huang Laoman. While escorting them past Siqiancun in Qujiang, they suddenly encountered the Luojing bandits. Yingyang's troops broke and scattered. Fen led his personal guard of more than a hundred men to fight the bandits, but munitions were exhausted and Fen was wounded. The bandits seized Huang Laoman and fled. Wrapping his wound, Fen wrote a memorial to Governor Ye Mingchen urgently stating that the bandit threat in the two Guang provinces was acute and that officials and people should be united and preparations made without delay. Several days later he died of his severe wounds. Condolences were granted according to regulation, and a special shrine was later built for him.
70
施作霖，浙江蕭山人。 拔貢，用知縣，發陝西。 咸豐三年，粵賊竄河南，奉檄督練勇防陝境，署城固縣知縣。 七年，河南角子山捻匪擾南陽府，將竄陝，巡撫曾望顏以作霖練勇有紀律，令防商南。 馳抵清油河，距武關三十里，賊已潛由天橋河陷武關，作霖偕候補同知曾兆蓉夜冒風雪抵頭條嶺，擊卻賊前敵。 越四道嶺，賊蜂至。 作霖奮下擊，義勇厲進，作霖手殲悍賊王黨。 餘賊卻拒守關，作霖直逼關前，賊復三面撲。 熸賊二十餘騎，賊攻愈猛。 作霖分隊擊，身受重創，力竭死。 家丁王建、義勇馬永剛等十三人皆死之。 賜卹，諡剛毅，賞世職，建專祠。
Shi Zuolin was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang. Selected as a tribute graduate, he was appointed magistrate and assigned to Shaanxi. In the third year of Xianfeng, when Guangdong rebels fled into Henan, he received orders to supervise the training of militia to defend the Shaanxi border and served as acting magistrate of Chenggu County. In the seventh year, Nien bandits from Jiaozishan in Henan harassed Nanyang Prefecture and were about to flee into Shaanxi. Governor Zeng Wangyan, seeing that Zuolin's militia training was disciplined, ordered him to defend Shangnan. He rushed to Qingyou River, thirty li from Wuguan Pass, but the bandits had already secretly taken Wuguan via Tianqiao River. Zuolin together with acting sub-prefect Zeng Zhaorong braved wind and snow by night to reach Toutiao Ridge and repulsed the bandits' vanguard. After crossing four ridges, the bandits swarmed up. Zuolin charged down fiercely to attack, and the militia pressed forward resolutely. Zuolin personally killed the fierce bandit Wang Dang. The remaining bandits retreated to hold the pass. Zuolin pressed straight to the pass, and the bandits again assaulted from three sides. He killed more than twenty mounted bandits, but the bandits' attack grew fiercer still. Zuolin divided his forces to strike, suffered grave wounds, and died when his strength was spent.
