Household retainers including Wang Jian and militiamen including Ma Yonggang, thirteen in all, also died. Condolences were granted, the posthumous title Gangyi was conferred, hereditary rank was awarded, and a special shrine was built.
71
韓體震，字省齋，河南夏邑人。 道光二十五年，捐州吏目，補直隸祁州吏目。 因父作謀任文安主簿，迴避，補山東德州吏目，捐升知縣。 以防堵功，獎開缺即選，選湖北通城縣。 防堵鄰境要隘出力，保同知。 同治元年，鄂督官文調赴軍營差委，嗣權孝感縣事。 孝感屢經殘破，城缺不完，體震修葺之，招鄉勇城守。 閏八月，捻匪大股分擾京山、應城一帶，闌入縣境，遂撲縣城。 體震與護軍統領舒保善因請入城同守，始解鞍，而賊由缺口入城，體震率勇巷戰，眾寡不敵，身受十傷，刀矛槍子無不備，大呼殺賊而死。 詔照知府例賜卹，給世職。
Han Tizhen, courtesy name Shengzhai, was a native of Xiayi in Henan. In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he purchased the post of prefectural clerk and was appointed clerk of Qizhou in Zhili. Because his father Zuo Mo held the post of registrar of Wen'an, he withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest, was appointed clerk of Dezhou in Shandong, and purchased advancement to magistrate. For merit in blocking and defending, he was rewarded with immediate selection when a vacancy opened and was selected for Tongcheng County in Hubei. For exertions in defending vital passes on the neighboring border, he was recommended for sub-prefect. In the first year of Tongzhi, Hubei Governor Guanwen summoned him to serve at the army camp; afterward he acted in charge of affairs in Xiaogan County. Xiaogan had been ravaged repeatedly and its city walls were incomplete. Tizhen repaired them and recruited local militia to garrison the city. In the intercalary eighth month a large Nien bandit force split off to harass the Jingshan and Yingcheng region, crossed into the county, and then assaulted the county seat. Tizhen and Guard Commander Shu Baoshan were invited into the city to defend together. He had just dismounted when the bandits entered through a breach. Tizhen led militia in street fighting, but they were outnumbered. He suffered ten wounds of every kind—blade, spear, and bullet—and cried out to kill bandits as he died. An edict granted condolences according to the prefect rank and awarded hereditary office.
72
德克登額，字靜庵，滿洲某旗人。 由筆帖式從將軍都興阿軍，累保至副都統記名。 嘗從攻廣濟，守營壘，不眠者七晝夜。 為人沉靜，溽暑不去長衣，每曰：「賊平即回家授徒，暇則垂釣黑龍江。 」又曰：「世受國恩，得一日授命疆場，則吾事畢矣！ 」與體震同守城，城陷，死之。
Deke Deng'e, courtesy name Jing'an, was a Manchu of a certain banner. Starting as a clerk, he followed General Duxing'a's army and was repeatedly commended until named for vice commander-in-chief. He once joined the attack on Guangji and, defending the encampment, went without sleep for seven days and nights. He was a man of calm disposition; even in sweltering heat he did not remove his long robe. He often said: "When the bandits are pacified I shall go home to teach pupils; in my leisure I shall fish on the Heilong River. " He also said: "Having received the state's grace through generations, should I one day receive my commission on the battlefield, my business is done! " He defended the city together with Tizhen; when the city fell, he died.
73
蔣嘉穀，順天大興籍，浙江山陰山。 以府經歷發貴州，旋保知縣。 咸豐三年，署荔波縣。 縣毗連粵西，粵氛近偪，土匪乘之。 嘉穀內守外禦，境內安堵。 始之任，獄多繁，囚半逆黨脅從，復有挾私誣告人從匪者。 嘉穀訊得實，俱決釋之。 時芻糧告匱，或以勸捐進，嘉穀曰：「民被蹂躪久矣，忍朘其生而激變乎？ 」事遂寢。 五年六月，水匪复叛，與廣匪合，約五六千人，薄城下，嘉穀募勇五百人擊退之。 時土匪遍地，餉需匱乏，嘉穀毀家募勇，妻陸氏亦出钅義釧佐軍，眾感奮，守愈堅。 以故附近州縣皆不保，獨荔波得存。 十月，賊復至，嘉穀部署城防，誓師出營於水堡，與賊遇，戰捷，賊小卻，後見師乏援，始無忌，麾眾並進。 嘉穀鏖戰終日，傷亡略盡，猶裹創刃賊，俄被執。 賊乘勝攻城，城以有備，卒不破。 嘉穀既陷賊，怒罵不屈。 賊束薪漬油遍體灼之，死而復甦，甦則罵，罵則復灼，如是數次，乃絕。 貴州巡撫蔣霨遠以嘉穀善政得民，力捍疆圉，被害尤慘。 奏入，卹世職。 士請捐建專祠，允之。
Jiang Jiagu was registered as a native of Daxing in Shuntian and was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang. Appointed as prefectural registrar and assigned to Guizhou, he was soon recommended for magistrate. In the third year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Libo County. The county bordered western Guangdong; as the Guangdong unrest drew near, local bandits took advantage. Jiagu defended within and resisted without, and within the jurisdiction all was secure. At the start of his tenure the prisons were crowded. Half the prisoners were coerced followers of rebels, and there were also those who brought false private accusations that others had joined the bandits. Jiagu interrogated and found the facts, and all were tried and released. At the time fodder and grain ran short, and some advised him to solicit donations and advance them. Jiagu said: "The people have long been trampled; can we bear to drain their livelihood and provoke revolt? " The matter was then dropped. In the sixth month of the fifth year the river bandits rebelled again and joined the Guangdong bandits, about five or six thousand strong. They pressed close to the city, but Jiagu recruited five hundred militiamen and drove them back. At the time local bandits were everywhere and pay and supplies were scarce. Jiagu ruined his household estate to raise militia, and his wife Lady Lu also contributed her hairpins and bracelets to aid the army. The people were stirred and inspired, and the defense grew firmer. For this reason nearby prefectures and counties all fell, but Libo alone survived. In the tenth month the bandits returned. Jiagu deployed the city's defenses, rallied the troops, and encamped at Shuibao. They met the bandits and fought victoriously, and the bandits fell back slightly. Later, seeing the army lacked reinforcements, they grew bold and commanded their masses to advance together. Jiagu fought fiercely all day until casualties were nearly complete. Still wrapping his wounds he slashed at bandits, but soon he was captured. The bandits pressed their victory to assault the city, but because it was well prepared, in the end it was not taken. Jiagu, having fallen into the bandits' hands, cursed them in rage and would not yield. The bandits bound firewood, soaked it in oil, and burned him all over. He died and revived; when he revived he cursed, and when he cursed they burned him again. Thus several times, and then he perished. Guizhou Governor Jiang Yuyuan reported that Jiagu had governed well and won the people, had stoutly defended the border, and had been murdered with especial cruelty. When the memorial was submitted, condolences and hereditary office were granted. The gentry requested to donate funds to build a special shrine, and this was approved.
74
鄧玲筠，字治薌，湖南寧鄉人。 舉人。 ，以知縣發貴州。 七年，擢知印江縣，時黔中苗、教匪充斥，匪酋以邪教蠱亂，民有黃號、白號等目，鄉團多叛應之。 玲筠銳意​​圖治，週巡轄境，與田更畬叟握手詢利病，手疏小冊，用是能摘發民隱，訟者神之。 思南賊熾，地連印江，亟行保甲法。 單騎詣各鄉，手自敦率，給門牌如式。 署紙尾十則：曰忤逆，曰習邪教，曰私結盟黨，曰劫掠，曰藏匪類，曰竊盜，曰容留娼妓，曰賭博，曰鬥毆生事，曰唆訟。 各擇士紳董之，犯者同甲勿與齒。 改悔者許具狀於各條下，加小印曰「自新」； 其頑抗及無人敢具保者治之。 且計月以驗紳董之能否，加勸懲焉。 又加意課士，割俸給書院餐錢，與講求正學，並及軍政，士皆畏愛之。 勸民修水利，立法詳盡易曉，或親履指示，不以勺水擾民。 邪教惑眾，為文告抉摘其謬，婦孺能解。 簡壯丁數百，親教之擊刺法。
Deng Lingyun, courtesy name Zhixiang, was a native of Ningxiang in Hunan. He was a provincial graduate. By appointment as magistrate he was assigned to Guizhou. In the seventh year he was promoted to magistrate of Yinjiang County. At the time Miao and religious rebels filled central Guizhou. Rebel chiefs used heterodox cults to stir disorder; the people had Yellow Banner, White Banner, and other factions, and local militia in many places rebelled in response. Lingyun was keen to govern well. He toured his jurisdiction weekly, shook hands with old farmers and field hands and inquired about their hardships and benefits, and personally wrote small booklets. By this means he could expose hidden grievances of the people, and litigants regarded him with awe. Rebels in Sinan were fierce and the territory connected with Yinjiang, so he urgently implemented the baojia system. He rode alone to each village, personally instructing and leading them, and issued door placards according to regulation. At the foot of the posted notice he set ten rules: filial impiety; practicing heterodox cults; forming secret societies; robbery and plunder; harboring bandits; theft; harboring prostitutes; gambling; brawling and making trouble; and inciting lawsuits. In each place gentry were chosen to supervise, and offenders were not to be counted among their baojia unit. Those who repented were permitted to submit written statements under each rule, with a small seal reading "Self-Renewed"; Those who were stubbornly resistant and for whom no one dared to stand surety were punished. Moreover he reckoned by the month to test the gentry supervisors' competence and added encouragement or punishment accordingly. He also devoted special attention to instructing scholars, cut his salary to provide meal money for the academy, lectured on orthodox learning, and also addressed military affairs. Scholars both feared and loved him. He urged the people to repair waterworks, made laws detailed and easy to understand, sometimes went in person to give instruction, and did not disturb the people over a spoonful of water. Heterodox cults deluded the masses; he wrote proclamations exposing their errors so that even women and children could understand. He selected several hundred strong young men and personally taught them thrust-and-strike methods.
75
是年十二月，賊陷思南，將犯印江。 印江故無城，出營於雲泮禦賊。 賊以書請假道，焚書，斬其人。 賊從間道襲治所，玲筠袖銅椎斃三賊。 賊環攻，復出銅鐧格鬥，賊莫敢近。 忽四山火起，乃突圍，抵銅仁乞師，得練總王士秀領五百人，一日夜行三百里。 民見玲筠歸，奮躍，復得壯士千餘，仍從至雲泮。 是日大霧，人馬對立不相見，譟而進。 賊奔，自相蹴蹋，墜崖死者無算。 复追百餘裡，戰中壩，戰螺生溪，戰袁家灣，皆捷。
In the twelfth month of that year the bandits took Sinan and were about to invade Yinjiang. Yinjiang originally had no city walls; he marched out and encamped at Yunpan to resist the bandits. The bandits sent a letter requesting passage; he burned the letter and executed the messenger. The bandits took a bypath to raid the magistrate's office; Lingyun killed three bandits with a copper mace hidden in his sleeve. The bandits surrounded and attacked; he again produced a copper truncheon and fought hand to hand, and the bandits did not dare approach. Suddenly fires rose on four mountains; he then broke out, reached Tongren to beg for troops, and obtained militia commander Wang Shixiu leading five hundred men. In one day and one night they marched three hundred li. When the people saw Lingyun return, they leaped with excitement. He again gathered more than a thousand stalwart men and still followed him to Yunpan. That day there was heavy fog; men and horses stood facing each other without seeing one another, and they advanced with a clamor. The bandits fled, trampling one another; those who fell from cliffs and died were beyond counting. He again pursued for more than a hundred li, fighting at Zhongba, at Luosheng Stream, and at Yuanjia Bay; all were victories.
76
八年春，知府令玲筠越境勦賊，知府先聞賊畏玲筠，立鄧字旗懾賊，故嚴檄三至。 縣民苦留，玲筠慨然曰：「郡守檄，縣令安敢違？ 且殺賊固​​無分畛域也。 」以千三百人往。 師次分水埡，賊混運糧者入營門，變作，眾驚潰。 玲筠親搏戰，飛石中首，手格殺一賊，足後被創，遂及於難，喪其元。 後軍聞失事，憤極，殊死鬥，殺聲與哭聲並，卒奪玲筠屍還。 乃樹「忠憤」幟，誓復仇，賊懼，退屯八十里。 喪歸，士民大慟，爭致賻賵。 有負販傭，挈錢四，將運鹽，悉以充賻。 或曰：「如爾家何？ 」傭哭曰：「公死，吾屬無葬所矣！ 何家為？ 」民懷其德，立祠祀之。 並刻遺集，曰鉅業堂稿。
In the spring of the eighth year the prefect ordered Lingyun to cross the border to suppress bandits. The prefect had earlier heard that the bandits feared Lingyun and raised a banner with the character Deng to intimidate them, hence three stern orders arrived. The county people begged him to stay. Lingyun said with emotion: "The prefect's order—how dare a county magistrate disobey? Moreover, killing bandits truly knows no boundary of territory. " He went with thirteen hundred men. The army halted at Fenshui Pass. Bandits mingled among grain carriers and entered the camp gate; a mutiny broke out, and the masses panicked and broke. Lingyun fought hand to hand himself. A flying stone struck his head; he killed one bandit in close combat, but his foot was wounded from behind. Thus he met calamity and lost his head. The rear guard, hearing of the disaster, were furious beyond measure. They fought to the death; cries of killing mingled with cries of weeping, and in the end they recovered Lingyun's corpse. They then raised the banner "Loyal Fury" and swore revenge. The bandits were afraid and withdrew to encamp eighty li away. When the funeral procession returned, scholars and people grieved greatly and vied to send condolence gifts. There was a porter who carried goods for hire; he had four strings of cash and was about to transport salt, but he gave it all for condolence gifts. Someone said: "What of your family? " The porter wept and said: "When the lord died, we of our sort have no place for burial! What of your family? " The people cherished his virtue and built a shrine to worship him. They also published his collected writings, titled *Juye Tang Drafts*.
77
承順，佟佳氏，漢軍正藍旗人。 由文生於咸豐四年隨其父甘肅寧夏鎮總兵定安出征湖北，累功擢至通判，發甘肅。 歷權寧夏鹽捕通判、平番縣事，授甘州撫彝通判，所至有聲。 同治元年，西寧撒回就撫，大吏以貴德廳孤懸大河以外，漢民與番、回雜處，治理不易，檄承順往署。 適番、回械鬥，承順為之平怨息爭，番、回悅服。 值河州回匪倡亂，甘、涼、寧、肅一帶響應，貴德回民洶洶欲動，承順勸導解散，以被難婦孺置署中別院，撫養數年。 有主者認還，無主者擇配。 由是漢、番感戴，回民亦懾其威。
Cheng Shun, of the Tongjia clan, was a member of the Han Military Plain Blue Banner. Starting as a civil licentiate, in the fourth year of the Xianfeng reign he followed his father Ding'an, regional commander of Ningxia in Gansu, on campaign to Hubei. For accumulated merit he was promoted to assistant prefect and sent to Gansu. He successively served in acting capacities as salt and bandit-suppression assistant prefect at Ningxia and in county affairs at Pingfan, was appointed assistant prefect for Yi affairs at Ganzhou, and wherever he went he won renown. In the first year of the Tongzhi reign, as the Salar Hui of Xining submitted to pacification, the high officials considered that Guide Department stood isolated beyond the great river, with Han people living mixed among Tibetans and Hui, making governance difficult. They ordered Cheng Shun to go and serve there in an acting capacity. Just then Tibetans and Hui clashed in armed fights. Cheng Shun settled their grievances and quelled the disputes, and both groups came to respect him. When Hui rebels at Hezhou raised rebellion and the regions of Gan, Liang, Ning, and Su all responded, the Hui of Guide grew turbulent and were on the verge of rising. Cheng Shun counselled and guided them to disperse, placed women and children who had suffered in calamity in a separate compound within his yamen, and nurtured them for several years. Those with masters were returned upon claim; those without were given husbands chosen for them. Thereupon the Han and Tibetans were moved with gratitude, and the Hui Muslims also feared his authority.
78
時西寧所屬各廳相繼淪陷，貴德一廳孤立賊中者六年。 城中回民暗結陝回謀亂，承順密調兵勇入城，嚴為之備。 回首馬朵三等率眾千餘人攻城，承順登陴抵禦，砲石雨下，斃賊頗多。 城內回民開門應賊，城遂陷。 承順率勇巷戰，身受重創，厲聲罵賊，賊怒，斷其左臂，罵愈厲； 复斷其右足，罵如故； 遂斷其首而支解之。 其弟議敘知縣崇順、監生吉順扶其母薩克達氏至屍所哭詈，皆遇害。 家丁李文忠等七名，同時死之。 事聞，卹贈道銜，給世職。
At that time the various departments subordinate to Xining fell one after another. Guide alone remained isolated among the rebels for six years. Inside the city, Hui people secretly joined with Shaanxi Hui to plot revolt. Cheng Shun secretly summoned troops and braves into the city and prepared strict defenses. The Hui leader Ma Duosan and others led more than a thousand men to attack the city. Cheng Shun climbed the ramparts to resist; cannonballs and stones fell like rain, and many rebels were killed. Inside the city the Hui opened the gates to assist the rebels, and the city then fell. Cheng Shun led his braves in street fighting. He suffered grave wounds and cursed the rebels in a fierce voice. The rebels were enraged and cut off his left arm, but his cursing grew fiercer; They again cut off his right foot; his cursing remained as before; Then they cut off his head and dismembered his body. His younger brother Chongshun, who had earned appointment as county magistrate through merit, the licentiate Jishun, and their mother, Lady Sakda, went to the corpse and wept and cursed; all were killed. Seven household servants including Li Wenzhong died at the same time. When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted the rank of circuit intendant and an hereditary office was awarded.
79
貴德士民復以死事狀赴都申訴，御史吳可讀疏言：「青海辦事大臣玉通疏報，祗及承順被害情形，猶惑於當時'回眾拘集漢民、勒寫官偪民反，漢、回同謀戕官'之說，後經查覆，於精忠大節，仍未述及。 在承順為國捐軀，光明俊偉，於原遂矣。 遺愛在民，漢、番男婦老幼呼為活佛。 誤觸其名，即童子皆呵禁之。 在朝廷為有臣，定安為有子，甘肅為有官。 闔門全節，允為一代完人，再懇優恤。 」光緒初元，陝甘總督左宗棠覆奏，謂：「承順死節奇偉，一時僅見。 綱常名義，不因品秩等差而別，則表揚較名位尊顯為尤亟。 請官為建祠，並予諡法，以勵人心。 」疏上，允之，諡勤愍。
The scholars and people of Guide again brought accounts of his death in service to the capital to petition. Censor Wu Kedu memorialized: "The Qinghai commissioner Yutong reported only the circumstances of Cheng Shun's murder, still influenced by the then-prevailing account that 'Hui masses detained Han people, forced them to write documents, officials compelled the people to rebel, and Han and Hui together conspired to kill the official'—yet after subsequent investigation and verification, his supreme loyalty and great integrity were still not mentioned. As for Cheng Shun, in dying for the state his conduct was bright and splendid—his original intent was fulfilled. His enduring kindness among the people: Han and Tibetan men and women, old and young, called him a Living Buddha. If anyone carelessly uttered his name, even children would rebuke and forbid it. For the court there was a loyal minister; for Ding'an there was a worthy son; for Gansu there was an upright official. The whole household preserved their integrity to the end—truly a complete person of an age—again earnestly requesting special posthumous honors. " In the first year of the Guangxu reign, Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Zuo Zongtang replied in memorial, saying: "Cheng Shun's death in loyalty was singular and grand—seldom seen in an age. The bonds of human relations and moral principle are not differentiated by rank and grade; thus commendation is even more urgent than status and eminence. Request that the state build a shrine for him and grant a posthumous title, to encourage hearts among the people. " When the memorial was submitted, it was approved; he was posthumously named Qinmin (Diligent and Compassionate).
80
托克清阿，字凝如，滿洲正藍旗人。 道光十四年舉人，大挑知縣，發甘肅，署環縣、安化知縣，及土魯番同知。 以清查事鐫級。 咸豐元年，捐復原官，補皋蘭。 時回、捻擾陝、甘，土匪聞風響應。 侍郎梁瀚治團練，疏薦之。 總督樂斌亦以其任事果敢，檄署秦州直隸州知州，尋實授。 同治二年，逆回竄甘南，州境戒嚴，托克清阿募壯勇，繕器械，力籌守禦。 賊竄秦安，率軍迎剿，屢挫賊。 賊糾大股至，眾寡不敵，力戰死之。 事聞，詔以道員從優議卹，秦州及本旗立專祠。 後秦州承其規畫，防禦嚴密，境獲安全。 四年，秦州士民以托克清阿忠貞孝友，慈惠嚴明，潔己愛民，禦災捍患，在任時民皆安業，賊不犯境。 遺愛餘威，實足固民心而寒賊膽，籥請加恩賜諡。 總督恩麟據以入告，特詔允之，予諡剛烈。
Tok Qing'a, styled Ningru, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner. In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the provincial examinations as a juren, was selected as county magistrate, was sent to Gansu, and served in acting capacities as magistrate of Huan and Anhua counties and as sub-prefect of Turfan. He was demoted one grade for matters uncovered in an audit. In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he purchased restoration to his original rank and was appointed to Gaolan. At that time Hui rebels and Nian bandits troubled Shaanxi and Gansu, and local bandits responded wherever they heard the news. Vice Minister Liang Han organized militia training and recommended him in a memorial. Governor-General Le Bin also, because of his bold and resolute conduct in office, ordered him to serve as acting prefect of Qinzhou directly administered prefecture, and he was soon given the formal appointment. In the second year of Tongzhi, rebellious Hui fled into southern Gansu. The prefectural territory was placed on alert. Tok Qing'a recruited strong braves, repaired weapons, and exerted himself to organize defense. When rebels fled into Qin'an, he led troops to meet them in suppression and repeatedly defeated the rebels. The rebels gathered a large force and arrived; outnumbered, he fought to the death. When the matter was reported, an edict ordered him to receive posthumous honors preferentially at the rank of circuit intendant. Qinzhou and his banner each established special shrines. Later Qinzhou carried forward his plans; defenses were strict and the territory was kept secure. In the fourth year, the scholars and people of Qinzhou submitted that Tok Qing'a was loyal, upright, filial, and friendly, benevolent yet strict and clear-sighted, personally incorruptible and loving toward the people, resisting disasters and warding off calamity. While in office the people all lived in peace, and rebels did not enter the territory. His enduring benevolence and residual awe truly sufficed to strengthen the hearts of the people and chill the courage of rebels; they pleaded for added grace and a posthumous name. Governor-General En Lin reported this upward, and a special edict approved it; he was given the posthumous name Ganglie (Firm and Fierce).
81
馮元吉，字景梅，浙江山陰人。 由供事議敘從九品，分廣西，歷署貴縣五山汛、凌雲平樂司巡檢。 道光二十八年，授宜山龍門巡檢。 咸豐元年，金田賊由武宣東鄉逃竄，都統烏蘭泰、提督向榮、總兵秦定三等節節追剿。 賊竄象州，兵勇不能禦，直至大樂墟，轉掠龍門。 元吉率鄉兵御之，戰敗，馳回署，衣冠坐堂皇，二子澍、溥侍立。 家人請暫避，元吉厲聲曰：「身為命官，不能殺賊安民，走避偷生，吾不為也！ 」麾二子出，皆痛哭不去。 賊至，父子抗罵，同遇害。 家丁嚴祿、夏玉俱死。 詔以元吉微員，從容盡節，澍、溥從父殉難，忠孝堪嘉。 贈鹽運使司知事銜，賞世職，建專祠，澍、溥附祀。
Feng Yuanji, styled Jingmei, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang. Starting from a clerk who earned appointment through merit to the rank of subordinate ninth grade, he was assigned to Guangxi and successively served in acting capacities as patrol inspector at Wushan garrison in Gui County and at Lingyun Pingle sub-bureau. In the twenty-eighth year of Daoguang he was appointed patrol inspector at Longmen in Yishan. In the first year of Xianfeng, the Jintian rebels fled from Dongxiang in Wuxuan. Commander-in-Chief Ulgeng, Regional Commander Xiang Rong, and General Qin Dingsan and others pursued them step by step. The rebels fled into Xiangzhou. Troops and braves could not repel them, and they reached Dale Market before turning to plunder Longmen. Yuanji led local militia to resist but was defeated. He galloped back to his office, put on formal dress and cap, and sat in the main hall, with his two sons Shu and Pu standing in attendance. His household asked him to withdraw for the moment. Yuanji said in a fierce voice: "As one holding an official commission, if I cannot kill rebels and secure the people, yet flee and steal my life—I will not do it! " He ordered his two sons out, but both wept bitterly and would not leave. When the rebels arrived, father and sons resisted and cursed; all were killed together. The household servants Yan Lu and Xia Yu both died. An edict stated that though Yuanji was a minor official, he calmly preserved his integrity to the end. Shu and Pu followed their father in martyrdom—filial piety and loyalty were truly admirable. He was posthumously granted the rank of Salt Transport Bureau clerk, awarded an hereditary office, and given a special shrine; Shu and Pu were enshrined alongside him.
82
平源，字沛霖，順天大興籍，浙江山陰人。 由吏員敘典史，發安徽。 咸豐二年，署懷寧縣典史，卹獄囚，嘗曰：「囚死於法，可也； 死於非法，不可也。 」眠食皆躬察之。 粵匪犯安慶，事急，囚譁，欲脫械去。 源至，囚曰：「此何時也，公胡弗自便？ 」源曰：「此若輩所以犯刑也，死可苟免耶？ 」囚曰：「公不去，囚何忍去？ 」俄而城陷，巡撫蔣文慶遇害，餘官皆走。 源獨冠服坐獄門外，賊至，脅之曰：「若降，官； 若不然，飲吾刃！ 」源曰：「刃則刃耳，吾豈受汝脅者？ 」賊曳至懷寧縣署外殺之，逮死罵不絕口。 安慶人思之，為立石於殉節處。
Ping Yuan, styled Peilin, registered in Daxing, Shuntian, and was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang. Starting as a clerk who earned appointment as jail warden, he was sent to Anhui. In the second year of Xianfeng he served as acting jail warden of Huaining County. He showed compassion to prisoners and once said: "That a prisoner die by law is acceptable; To die outside the law is not acceptable. " He personally inspected their sleeping and eating. When the Guangdong rebels attacked Anqing and the situation grew urgent, the prisoners clamored and wished to remove their shackles and flee. When Yuan arrived, a prisoner said: "What moment is this—why do you not save yourself, sir? " Yuan said: "Is this not why you people committed crime in the first place—can death be escaped through cowardice? " The prisoner said: "If you do not leave, sir, how could we prisoners bear to leave? " Before long the city fell. Governor Jiang Wenqing was killed, and the remaining officials all fled. Yuan alone put on cap and robe and sat outside the prison gate. When rebels arrived they threatened him, saying: "If you submit, office; If not, drink our blade! " Yuan said: "Blade is blade—I am not one to be threatened by you! " The rebels dragged him outside the Huaining county yamen and killed him; until death his curses did not cease. The people of Anqing remembered him and set up a stone tablet at the place of his martyrdom.
83
時又有張寶華者，為望江縣典史。 聞城陷，視其妻賈氏自經畢，冠服坐堂上罵賊，死。 華陽鎮巡檢王泗同時殉難，盱眙縣典史週來豫後於九年助守縣城，力戰墜馬死。
At that time there was also Zhang Baohua, jail warden of Wangjiang County. When he heard the city had fallen, after seeing his wife Lady Jia hang herself, he put on cap and robe, sat in the hall cursing the rebels, and died. Wang Si, patrol inspector of Huayang town, died at the same time. Zhou Laiyu, jail warden of Xuyi County, later in the ninth year aided in defending the county seat, fought fiercely, fell from his horse, and died.
84
餘寶錕，江西德化人。 附貢生，捐知縣。 ，選授浙江景寧縣，以才力不及降調。 复捐縣丞，發貴州。 三月，署麻哈州吏目。 四月，仁懷縣教匪楊漋喜竄麻哈，隨知州何鋌擊卻之。 尋盜魁陳大陸糾苗匪來犯，复隨鋌出戰。 賊退，遂率眾攻拔下司岩、下雞場等處，扼茅坪山，悉力堵禦。 未幾，賊聚益眾，勢不能敵。 退州城，賊旋陷都勻府。 提督孝順兵至茅坪被圍，寶錕率團兵隨總兵佟攀梅援剿，圍解。 自是無日不戰，互有勝負。 巡撫蔣霨遠檄雲南降將陳得功隨孝順攻克都勻，進援麻哈，官軍勢復振。 得功旋叛去，孝順軍潰，賊大股圍州城三日，寶錕率鄉兵登陴固守，賊不​​得逞。 七年，城中糧匱，兵益單，寶錕自誓與城存亡。 八年正月，賊悉眾來攻，寶錕出北門迎敵，不利，入城，賊已自他門入。 寶錕持矛巷戰，賊不忍害，揮令去。 寶錕怒罵，掣矛刺之，賊奪矛還刺，死之。
Yu Baokun was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi. A supplementary tribute student, he purchased appointment as county magistrate. He was selected and appointed to Jingning County in Zhejiang, but was demoted for insufficient ability. He again purchased appointment as assistant magistrate and was sent to Guizhou. In the third month he served as acting clerical officer of Mahazhou. In the fourth month, the teaching-cult rebel Yang Zhangxi of Renhuai County fled into Mahazhou. He joined Prefect He Ting in repelling them. Soon after, the bandit chief Chen Dalu gathered Miao rebels to attack. Again he followed Ting into battle. When the rebels withdrew, he then led troops to capture Xiabasi Rock, Xiajichang, and other places, held Maoping Mountain, and exerted every effort to block and defend. Before long the rebels gathered in greater numbers; the force could not be matched. They withdrew to the prefectural city; the rebels soon took Duyun Prefecture. Regional Commander Xiaoshun's troops reached Maoping and were besieged. Baokun led militia with General Tong Panmei in relief suppression, and the siege was lifted. From then on there was fighting every day, with victories and defeats on both sides. Governor Jiang Weiyuan ordered the Yunnan defector Chen Degong to follow Xiaoshun in recovering Duyun and advance to relieve Mahazhou. The government army's momentum revived. Degong soon betrayed them and left; Xiaoshun's army broke. A large rebel force besieged the prefectural city for three days. Baokun led local braves up the ramparts to hold firm, and the rebels could not succeed. In the seventh year, grain in the city ran short and troops grew ever fewer. Baokun vowed to live or die with the city. In the first month of the eighth year, the rebels came with their full strength. Baokun went out the north gate to meet the enemy, fared poorly, and entered the city—but the rebels had already entered through other gates. Baokun fought through the streets with a spear. The rebels could not bear to harm him and waved him away. Baokun cursed in fury, drew his spear to stab them. The rebels seized the spear and stabbed back, killing him.
85
王汝揆，甘肅伏羌人。 道光二十年舉人，揀選知縣，親老改教職。 咸豐間，授平涼縣教諭。 同治元年，陝西回匪竄乾鳳，偪甘肅境，汝揆上書平慶涇道萬金鏞曰：「賊西偪鳳翔，必分黨由汧、隴間道趨秦安東北，構煽醜類。 宜及其未至，扼險嚴防。 不然，內應且四起，平涼擾則靈、固、狄、河等州縣亦危矣！ 」言未及用，賊尋由固關逾隴，張家川、蓮花城土回應之，陷鹽茶及固原，金鏞死之，平涼戒嚴。 汝揆議盡毀城外民舍，無令賊倚為障蔽，議不行。 未幾，賊圍平涼，汝揆協同守令，督率生徒，登陴固守，衣不解帶者六閱月。 一日，偵西北二路賊少可擊，謁知府田增壽請率壯士縋城出剿，又不許。 二年，賊匿民舍掘地道，納火藥轟之，城遂陷。 人皆泣曰：「早從教諭言，事豈至此乎？ 」汝揆還署，易朝服，北向叩首訖，妻汪氏暨女一、孫女一皆死，乃從容就縊於孔廟鍾虡以殉。
Wang Rukui was a native of Fuqiang in Gansu. In the twentieth year of Daoguang he passed as a juren, was selected as county magistrate, but because his parents were elderly changed to an educational post. During the Xianfeng era he was appointed instructor of Pingliang County. In the first year of Tongzhi, Shaanxi Hui rebels fled into Qian and Feng. Pressing the Gansu border, Rukui wrote to Circuit Intendant Wan Jinyong of Ping-Qing-Jing circuit: "The rebels press west on Fengxiang; they will certainly split a party to take the byways through Qian and Long toward the northeast of Qin'an, inciting evil elements. It is fitting, before they arrive, to hold the passes and defend strictly. Otherwise internal collaborators will rise on all sides; if Pingliang is disturbed, then Lingtai, Guyuan, Didao, Hezhou, and other prefectures and counties will also be imperiled! Before his advice could be taken, the rebels crossed into Longyou through Guguan Pass. Muslims at Zhangjiachuan and Lianhuacheng rose in support. Yanchai and Guyuan fell, Jin Yong was killed, and Pingliang went on alert. Rukui proposed tearing down all houses outside the walls so the rebels could not use them for cover, but the plan was rejected. Soon the rebels besieged Pingliang. Rukui joined the defending officials, led the students onto the walls, and for six months never unbuckled his belt. One day scouts reported fewer rebels on the northwest and west routes. He asked Prefect Tian Zengshou to let him lead men down ropes from the wall to attack, but was refused again. In the second year the rebels hid in houses, tunneled under the wall, packed the tunnel with gunpowder, and blasted the city open. Everyone wept and said: "If only we had listened to the instructor sooner, how could it have come to this?" Rukui returned to the yamen, put on court robes, and kowtowed to the north. After his wife Lady Wang, a daughter, and a granddaughter had all died, he calmly hanged himself on the bell frame in the Confucian temple.
86
汝揆性質實，敦孝友。 居親喪，不入內，不御酒肉。 弟印揆，客西寧久，音信乏絕，汝揆往尋之，風雪中徒步千餘裡，卒挈其弟以歸。 平生肆力於經籍，家居課徒，以窮經為急，輒點勘善本授之，勗以立品敦行。 其官平涼，亦以是為教。 期年，訟庭無士子跡。 當城未陷之先兩月，有門人馳書勸引疾歸，謂可免難。 汝揆曰：「無疾而稱疾，是欺也； 食祿而苟免，非義也。 」乃為書與戚友訣，略曰：「我生不辰，逢天癉怒，向者耳聞之，今則目睹之。 平郡自二月以來，圍困日迫，飛書告急，援兵無一至者。 汝揆妻、女，行當自盡，決不受辱於賊手。 死者士之終，今誠獲死所矣。 惟官卑不得展一籌以報國，死有餘憾耳。 」三年，官軍克平涼，總督楊岳斌請優恤。 六年，總督穆圖善疏陳汝揆死事狀，請照陣亡例議卹，贈國子監助教銜，給世職，又命於本籍建祠，以從死之妻、女等附祀。
Rukui was sincere by nature and devoted to filial piety and brotherly duty. While mourning his parents he did not enter the inner quarters and abstained from wine and meat. His younger brother Yinhuai had long been away at Xining without word. Rukui went to find him, walked more than a thousand li through wind and snow, and finally brought him home. He devoted his life to the classics. At home he taught students, stressing mastery of the texts, collating fine editions for them, and urging them to build character and live uprightly. At Pingliang he taught in the same way. Within a year no student appeared before his court on legal matters. Two months before the city fell, a student wrote urging him to plead illness and go home to escape disaster. Rukui said: "To claim illness when I am not ill would be deceit;" "to draw a salary yet save myself at all costs would be wrong." He then wrote farewell letters to family and friends, saying in part: "I was born under an unlucky star and now meet Heaven's wrath. What I once only heard, I now see with my own eyes." "Since the second month Pingliang has been besieged ever more tightly. Urgent appeals have gone out, yet no relief has come." "My wife and daughters will soon take their own lives rather than suffer dishonor at the rebels' hands." "Death is a scholar's proper end; today I have truly found my place to die." "Only because my rank was low could I offer no plan to repay the state; that is my one regret in dying." In the third year government troops recovered Pingliang, and Governor Yang Yuebin asked for special honors. In the sixth year Governor Mutushan described Rukui's death in service and asked for honors under the regulations for death in battle: the nominal rank of Imperial Academy assistant instructor, a hereditary office, and a shrine in his home district with his wife, daughters, and others who died with him honored there as well.
